Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionising this field by enabling rapid, precise, and data-driven enzyme design. Machine learning and deep learning models such as AlphaFold2, RoseTTAFold, ProGen, and ESM-2 accurately predict enzyme structure, stability, and catalytic function, facilitating rational mutagenesis and optimisation.

title: Tailoring PLA/Gelatin Film Properties for Food Packaging Using Deep Eutectic Solvents
creator: M. Cidália R. Castro, João Pereira, Mara Pires André, Pedro Pereira, Vasco Cruz, Pedro Veiga Rodrigues, Ana Vera Machado
description: This work investigates the modification of poly(lactic acid) (PLA) film properties for food packaging applications through the incorporation of modified gelatin (Gel-mod) and a choline chloride/glycerol deep eutectic solvent (DES). PLA/Gel-mod/DES materials were melt-processed and evaluated with respect to structure, morphology, thermal and mechanical behavior, processability, wettability, barrier performance, and compostability.

title: Corn Stover for Food Applications: Approaches, Advances and Insights
creator: Mariana Ochoa-Castaño, Nicolás Montoya-Escobar, Jorge Andrés Velásquez-Cock, Catalina Gómez-Hoyos
description: Corn processing generates substantial volumes of agricultural by-products, collectively referred to as corn stover, comprising husks, cobs, stalks, leaves, and silks. Although rich in bioactive compounds, these by-products are still predominantly destined for low-value uses such as landfilling and open-field burning.

title: Unqualified Advice and Product Promotions: Analysis of Health and Nutrition Content on Social Media Consumed by Young Adults
creator: Sophie Evans, Kelly Lambert, Adrian Dinale, Myah Quinn, Denelle Cosier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: This study investigated the relationship between time spent on social media and eating behaviours among young Australian adults. It also examined the types of content discussed and linguistic styles used by health and nutrition content creators on Instagram. Methods: Young adults (aged 18–30 years) who reported viewing social media for nutrition or health content were recruited to complete a self-administered, cross-sectional survey.

title: High-Accuracy Chicken Breed Identification Using Microsatellite Genotype Data and AutoGluon Framework
creator: Rajaonarison Faniriharisoa Maxime Toky, Sutthisak Sukhamsri, Sadeep Medhasi, Trifan Budi, Thitipong Panthum, Worapong Singchat, Kornsorn Srikulnath
description: Simple SummaryIdentifying chicken breeds correctly is important for conserving local breeds and improving breeding programs. However, many breeds look very similar, making visual identification difficult and sometimes inaccurate. In this study, genetic information from several chicken populations was used to train a machine learning model to recognize breed patterns.

title: An Econometric Analysis of Climatic Effects on Total Factor Productivity Across U.S. Dairy Counties
creator: Kamil Bora Bolat, Merve Bolat, Boris E. Bravo-Ureta
description: Simple SummaryHigh-yielding dairy cows face increasing heat stress due to climate change. Our study analyzed over four decades of data from U.S. dairy counties to understand the economic implications of this challenge. Using a detailed statistical model, we separated the effects of technological progress from climatic pressures on total factor productivity.

title: Lung Ultrasound for Pleural Effusion in Cancer Patients: Advanced Ultrasound for Pleural Lesions—A Narrative Review
creator: Hajo Findeisen, Christian Görg, Viktoria Zies, Michael Ludwig, Christoph F. Dietrich, Amjad Alhyari, Corinna Trenker-Burchert
description: Simple SummaryLung ultrasound is typically the first-line imaging modality for detecting or excluding pleural effusion. Malignant pleural effusion represents an advanced disease stage, with imaging and pathology playing central roles in diagnosis. This review summarizes recent advances in lung ultrasound, particularly contrast-enhanced ultrasound and elastography, which hold promise for improving the diagnostic workup in malignant pleural effusion. 1.

title: g-C3N4/CeO2/Bi2O3 Dual Type-II Heterojunction Photocatalysis Self-Cleaning Coatings: From Spectral Absorption Modulation to Engineering Application Characterization
creator: Shengchao Cui, Run Cheng, Feng Sun, Huishuang Zhao, Hang Yuan, Qing Si, Mengzhe Ai, Weiming Du, Kan Zhou, Yantao Duan, Wenke Zhou
description: To enhance the purification of exhaust gas, a g-C3N4/CeO2/Bi2O3 dual type-II heterojunction photocatalysis was designed and prepared to suppress the recombination of electron–hole pairs and improve light energy utilization. The dual type-II heterojunction structure effectively reduced the bandgap (Eg) from 2.5 eV to 2.04 eV, thereby extending the light absorption of photocatalysis into the visible region.

title: Interdisciplinary interactive blended learning concept in times of a pandemic – pain medicine “totally digital”
creator: Lisa Schramm, Patrick Friedrich, Jürgen Schüttler, Björn Lütcke
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction: Pain medicine is located in different sections of the medical curriculum. In the pandemic situation, an online teaching concept for Q14 which includes several disciplines had to be developed. The goal of the project was to create a fully digitized learning platform for the cross-sectional area Q14 that allows all participating disciplines to address the various learning goals without losing a practical component.Project description: First, the students' expectations regarding education in the field of pain medicine were recorded by means of

title: Intraoperative bradycardia leading to cardiac arrest during anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) in a morbidly obese patient—a rare complication and management strategy: a case report
creator: Worawich Kraipindakul, Teerachat Tanasansomboon, Wicharn Yingsakmongkol, Weerasak Singhatanadgige, Vit Kotheeranurak, Worawat Limthongkul
description: BackgroundIntraoperative bradycardia leading to cardiac arrest is a rare and serious complication during anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) surgeries. This case report presents a unique and previously undocumented instance of bradycardia progressing to asystole during an ALIF, highlighting the importance of autonomic nervous system involvement and intraoperative vigilance.

title: Single‐Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals an Inflammatory Antigen‐Presenting Macrophages Subtype Drive Vitiligo Pathogenesis Through STAT1‐Mediated Dual Mechanisms
creator: Ruozhou Qi, Min Huang, Ziyi Lin, Huanhuan Deng, Rule Sa, Yi Chen, Guangshan Chen, Xingwu Duan, Liu Jinhui
description: BackgroundVitiligo is a common depigmentary disorder characterized by progressive melanocyte (MEL) loss. While T‐cell activation is central to its pathogenesis, the role of macrophages remains poorly understood. This study characterizes macrophage heterogeneity and function in vitiligo using single‐cell transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation.MethodsWe analyzed single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) data from healthy and vitiligo‐affected skin to identify macrophage subpopulations.

title: Effects of kinesiology taping leggings on exercise performance and physiological responses during CrossFit training in women aged 20–30 years
creator: Joon-Hee Kim, Sung-Heum Um, Jae-Suk Lee
description: This study examined the effects of kinesiology taping leggings on exercise performance and physiological responses during CrossFit training in women aged 20–30 years. A randomized crossover design was employed with 42 healthy participants. Each participant completed two 3-week training periods wearing either taping leggings or regular leggings, separated by a 2-week washout period.

title: Protective effects of Exocarpium Citri Grandis against sepsis-induced acute lung injury via PANoptosis inhibition
creator: Zaibin Xu, Kongyan Wang, Huiyu Hu, Yan Chen, Yi Qiu, Jiazhong Cai, Weirong Li, Zhuohui Luo, Hang Li, Jiawen Huang
description: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening condition with high mortality, driven by dysregulated inflammation and programmed cell death. Exocarpium Citri Grandis (ECG), which refers to the dried outer rind of the Rutaceae plant Citrus grandis ‘Tomentosa’ or Citrus grandis (L.

title: Suture Fixation Versus Screw Fixation in Pediatric Tibial Eminence Fractures: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Reoperation Rates
creator: Ahmed Elnewishy, Ziad El Menawy, Mohamed Zahed, Mahmoud Elmesalmi, Nour Elnaggar, Farouk Ahmed, Mahmoud Odeh, Mohamed Elgamal
description: Suture fixation (SF) has gained prominence as a physeal-sparing alternative to screw fixation (SCF) in the operative management of pediatric tibial eminence fractures, aiming to reduce hardware-related complications while maintaining joint stability. This meta-analysis evaluated clinical and functional outcomes comparing SF with SCF in skeletally immature patients.

title: Therapeutic potential of stem cells in pediatric neurology: Insights from clinical trials
creator: Daniel Bou Najm, Saada Alame
description: Pediatric neurological disorders comprise diverse conditions that impair nervous system function in children and contribute substantially to global disease burden. Stem cell therapy has become a promising treatment in neurology due to the cells' ability to self‐renew, ensuring a continuous supply of cells.

title: Biomarkers Detecting the Activity of ANCA‐Associated Vasculitis: A Systematic Literature Review
creator: L Baas, R M Krol, E C Hagen, J Spierings, Y K O Teng, C A Koelman, H H F Remmelts, David Kershaw
description: IntroductionAnti‐neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)–associated vasculitis (AAV) encompasses a group of rare systemic autoimmune diseases characterized by inflammation of small‐ and medium‐sized blood vessels. Despite the efficacy of immunosuppressive therapy in achieving disease remission, a significant proportion of patients experience relapses, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers to monitor disease activity.

title: Rituximab for Early‐Onset Juvenile Dermatomyositis Complicated by Interstitial Lung Disease
creator: M. Olszewska, E. Mężyk, M. Kurbiel, W. Kmiecik, D. Turowska-Heydel, M. Sobczyk, Z. Żuber
description: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is the most common inflammatory myopathy in children. Among its various multisystem manifestations, JDM‐associated interstitial lung disease (JDM‐ILD) can cause significant disability and mortality. Data on the management of JDM‐ILD are limited. However, rituximab can be an effective and safe option not only for refractory cases but also for initial treatment.

title: First record of the adult of Cymbalcloeon confirming its position in Baetidae (Insecta, Ephemeroptera)
creator: Ningning Wang, Di Wang, Jean-Luc Gattolliat, Chanaporn Suttinun, Changfa Zhou
description: BackgroundThe nymphs of Cymbalcloeon sartorii Suttinun et al., 2020 present several unusual characters such as having only three pairs of ventral gills. The imaginal stage of this recently described genus remains unknown.New informationIn Spring 2025, tens of nymphs as well as morphologically and molecularly associated adults of this species were collected in southwestern China.

title: ﻿Two new species of Penicillium (Eurotiales, Aspergillaceae) and the first record of P. danzhouense from mangrove sediment in Thailand, with notes on antibacterial activity
creator: Vassana Supapongsri, Ananya Sahathippayakul, Wanchat Sirisarn, Mohit Chand, Jui-Yu Chou, Piyangkun Lueangjaroenkit
description: ﻿AbstractTwo novel species of Penicillium, comprising P. chanthaburiensesp. nov. and P. buranakarlianumsp. nov., were isolated from mangrove sediment collected at the King Rama IX International Mangrove Botanical Garden in Chanthaburi Province, Thailand. Morphological characterization combined with multilocus phylogenetic analyses of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS), β-tubulin (TUB), calmodulin (CaM), and RNA polymerase II second largest subunit (RPB2) genes placed P.

title: Simultaneous Total Hip Arthroplasty and Plate Fixation for Ipsilateral Subtrochanteric Fracture Following Femoral Neck Osteosynthesis
creator: Hirokazu Takai, Ryota Moroi, Masato Shiroma, Kensuke Miyazaki, Shingo Hama, Seiko Takai, Chihiro Hayai, Tomoki Takahashi
description: BackgroundSubtrochanteric fracture is a recognized complication following osteosynthesis for femoral neck fractures, typically occurring within 1–2 months postoperatively. At the time of onset, incomplete healing of the femoral neck fracture often results in a complex fracture configuration that poses challenges for management.

title: Transnasal Endoscopic Approach via Inferolateral Periorbital Periosteal Line for the Posterior Orbital Region
creator: Teru Ebihara, Kazuhiro Omura, Iori Sano, Nobuyoshi Otori
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We report a minimally invasive transnasal endoscopic approach via the inferolateral periorbital periosteal line, which allows for safer surgery in the inferolateral orbital region without external incisions. This method enables better visibility while preserving physiological function and reducing cosmetic risks by minimizing fat deviation and avoiding problems such as ocular compression and orbital bone resection commonly encountered in open and transorbital surgery. This technique may be an optimal alternative or complement to traditional open surgery.

title: A Novel Ultrasound Assessment Technique of the Ulnar Collateral Ligament to Account for the Valgus Stress Effect of Gravity on the Medial Elbow
creator: Ricardo E Colberg, Tomas F Vega, Jeremy Towns, Alex F Yates, Brody Westbrooks, Sydney Carlson, Glenn S Fleisig, Matthew P Ithurburn
description: Background:The ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) of the elbow is commonly injured in baseball athletes. When assessed in the supine abducted and externally rotated (ABER) position using stress ultrasonography (sUS), even before applying a valgus load, gravity pulls on the forearm, creating an initial valgus load that may distort the resting joint space measurement.

title: A Review of Acupuncture for Allergic Disorders: Modulation of Mast Cell Regulation via Inflammatory Pathway Suppression and Cytokine Balance
creator: Yuan Li, Ying Meng, Chen Chen, Kexin Jiang, Ji Li
description: ObjectiveMast cells drive allergic diseases (asthma, rhinitis, dermatitis) via degranulation and pro-inflammatory mediator release. This review explores acupuncture’s role in modulating mast cells to alleviate allergic symptoms.MethodsWe screened PubMed and Embase databases from January 2010 to January 2025 to search for published studies.

title: Gamification Strategies in Digital Health Interventions for Attention Rehabilitation in Stroke Survivors: A Systematic Review
creator: Andri Nugraha, Cecep Eli Kosasih, Iqbal Pramukti, Vitriana Biben
description: BackgroundStroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, with attentional deficits affecting most survivors and limiting independence, activities of daily living (ADL), and quality of life. Conventional rehabilitation often lacks engagement and accessibility, which underscores the need for innovative strategies. Digital health interventions incorporating gamification may enhance attentional rehabilitation. However, the evidence remains limited.

title: Relationship Between Monocyte-to-High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Ratio and Visceral Obesity in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Ye Hu, Jia Zheng, Yubo Xing, Yingxiang Song, Xiaohong Wu
description: PurposeThe study aimed to explore the relationship between the monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) and visceral fat area (VFA) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).Patients and MethodsA total of 2156 patients with T2DM who received medical treatment at Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital participated in this study.

title: Appropriate CT Technology to Fully Assess a Palatal Myoepithelioma
creator: Xiang Zhuang, Hongliang Li, Qingyu Ji
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Teaching point: Palatal myoepithelioma has almost pathognomonic progressive heterogeneous delayed enhancement on contrast CT, and a dedicated software application contributes to the surgical planning through hyper‑realistic rendering (HRR) 3D delineation of tumor extent/spatial relationships with critical adjacent structures. Case History A 46‑year‑old woman presented with a two‑year history of a painless palatal nodule, which she had initially disregarded due to the absence of symptoms.

title: How Dark Stars and Three Stripes Can Aid in Characterization of Muscle Sarcoidosis?
creator: Rob Vernelen, Charlotte Vanhoenacker, Filip Vanhoenacker
description: Teaching point: The clues to the correct diagnosis of muscle sarcoidosis on MRI are the typical ‘dark star’ sign in the axial plane and the ‘three‑stripe’ sign in the longitudinal plane.Keywords: sarcoidosis, muscle sarcoidosis, MRI, US, dark star, three stripes Case History A 36‑year‑old male presented with swollen calves and multiple palpable nodules in the calf muscles.

title: First Suspected Case of Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease in Syria
creator: Hamed Tarboosh, Raghed Mansour, Noor Haidar, Pierre Ghulam, Reem Gergy, Faten Nafla
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Prion diseases are rare, fatal neurodegenerative disorders caused by misfolded proteins. Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob Disease (sCJD) is the most common form and develops without any identifiable triggers. This case report documents the first probable diagnosis of sCJD in Syria, involving a 72-year-old woman who presented with depressive symptoms for several months before rapidly deteriorating, and eventually succumbing to complications of the disease.

title: Development of Predictive Models for Long-Term Endoscopic Response to Ustekinumab in Crohn’s Disease Based on Plasma Proteomics
creator: Chenchen Wu, Jiawen Zheng, Xin Qian, Chunyan Peng, Fan Zhou, Lei Wang
description: PurposeUstekinumab (UST) is effective for Crohn’s disease (CD), yet reliable biomarkers for predicting long-term response remain scarce. This study aimed to identify novel plasma proteomic biomarkers and develop predictive models for long-term endoscopic response to UST therapy in patients.MethodsBaseline plasma inflammatory proteins were profiled using the Olink platform in 40 CD patients treated with UST (20 responders, 20 non-responders).

creator: Jin Hwan Kim, Sung Tan Cho, Byung Jik Kim, Su Whi Chae, Wongthawat Liawrungrueang

Study design and statistical approach We agree that our retrospective design represents level III evidence and that multivariable analysis could further elucidate predictors of surgical conversion.

title: Safety outcomes of trazodone versus antipsychotics for delirium after hospital admission in adults aged 65 years and older: a nationwide cohort study using a target trial emulation framework
creator: Chun-Ting Yang, James M Wilkins, Kevin T Pritchard, Qiaoxi Chen, Xiaojuan Liu, Dae Hyun Kim, Kueiyu Joshua Lin
description: SummaryBackgroundTrazodone has emerged as a potentially safer alternative to atypical antipsychotic medications for managing delirium-related symptoms in older adults after hospital admission. This study aimed to compare safety outcomes in older adults who were prescribed trazodone versus atypical antipsychotic medication after hospital discharge.

title: Navigating goals of care discussion in palliative care: A qualitative study applying Bourdieu’s theory of practice
creator: Haiyang Lin, Shiyong Tan, Yufei Huang, Haojie Duan, Yumei Li, Yanping Hao
description: Background:Nowadays, effective communication has become indispensable with the increasing prevalence of advanced life-limiting diseases. Goals of care discussion (GOCD) align care with patients’ preferences and improve care quality.Objectives:This paper probes deep into the dilemmas and summarizes strategies of medical staff conducting GOCD from the viewpoint of human-environment interaction.Design:Qualitative study comprising semi-structured in-depth interviews.

title: Exploring Methods of Adjusting VO2max for Body Size to Estimate Aerobic Capacity in People Presenting for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery
creator: Rebecca Dostan, Sara Slayman, Belinda Durey, Brett Tarca, Justin Bessell, Kade Davison
description: BackgroundIn perioperative settings exercise testing can be used to assess a patient's physical fitness, with VO2max used as a marker to indicate fitness and subsequent risk of adverse surgical outcomes. However, the commonly used reporting methods of VO2max may be problematic in populations with excessive FM such as those awaiting MBS for obesity.

title: Speed Breeding Transgenic American Chestnut Trees Toward Restoration
creator: Thomas Klak, Hannah Pilkey, Virginia G May, Dakota Matthews, Allison D Oakes, Ek Han Tan, Andrew E Newhouse
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The American chestnut ( Castanea dentata ) was a dominant, foundational forest canopy tree in eastern North America until an imported chestnut blight (caused by Cryphonectria parasitica ) rendered it functionally extinct across its native range. Biotechnological approaches have the potential to help restore the species, but field‐based breeding advances are hampered by long generation times, ≤ 50% transgene inheritance, and regulatory restrictions on outdoor breeding of transgenic trees. Self‐incompatibility and flowering phenology further limit generational advances and field testing of chestnuts.

title: Study on Floral Syndrome and Breeding System of an Endangered Species Rhododendron nymphaeoides
creator: Jun Luo, Meng Chen, Haiyan Long, Yuting Zhu, Congjun Yuan, Kai Hu, Jin Chen, Run Liu, Xiaoyong Dai, Fangjun Ding
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Rhododendron nymphaeoides is a plant belonging to the genus Rhododendron (Rhododendron Linn.) and the subsection Fortunea. Although this species is clearly listed as endangered (with an endangered status of EN) by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List, the Red List of Rhododendrons, the Red List of China's Higher Plants, and the Threatened Species List of China's Higher Plants, the question of whether its mating system is self‐pollinating or cross‐pollinating remains a perplexing issue that hinders the conservation and

title: The Role of miR‐138 in Cardiovascular Diseases
creator: Taidou Jiang, Bijian Wang, Zhi Luo, Ying Xia, Yaoyu Qi, Sha Luo, Binyan Lang, Bolan Zhang, Shuzhan Zheng, Baisakhi Banerjee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cardiovascular disease (CVD) represents the foremost cause of morbidity and mortality globally, posing a significant threat to human health. The regulatory mechanisms underlying CVD are still not fully elucidated. MicroRNA (miRNA), a class of noncoding short‐chain RNA molecules, modulates individual genes or gene networks by binding to the complementary sequences of specific target genes, thereby influencing various biological processes including cell genesis, metabolism, proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis. Among these, miR‐138 plays a significant role in the onset and progression of CVDs.

title: Positive Indirect Antiglobulin Test in Adult Patients With Primary Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia: Clinical Significance and Prognostic Effect on Response to Corticosteroids
creator: Mahmoud Husni Ayesh (Haj Yousef), Muna Al-Khalayleh, Khaled A. Abu Hmdeh, Mustafa M. Hayajneh, Weam El-Sheyab
description: BackgroundPrimary warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (PWAIHA) is a subtype of autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) characterized by premature destruction of red blood cells (RBCs) due to autoantibodies, typically immunoglobulin G (IgG), the cornerstone of which is a positive direct antiglobulin test.

title: One‐Year Clinical Evaluation of the Horizontal Mattress Sling Suture for Aesthetic Crown Lengthening
creator: Najla S. Kasabreh, Hearos A. Bedros, Dimitris N. Tatakis
description: IntroductionIn aesthetic crown lengthening (ACL) surgery, conventional suturing techniques, such as interrupted or vertical mattress sutures, involve piercing both buccal and palatal tissues. This preliminary case series introduces a new suturing approach, “the horizontal mattress sling suture” (HMSS), that eliminates the need to pierce palatal tissues and thus avoids the requirement for palatal anesthesia.

title: Scientific Opinion on the application of physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modelling for the quantitative in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (QIVIVE) of developmental neurotoxicity in vitro battery (DNT IVB) data for pesticide active substances
creator: EFSA Panel on Plant Protection Products and their Residues (PPR), Tamara Coja, Pauline Adriaanse, Judy Choi, Antonio Finizio, Maeva Giraudo, Thomas Kuhl, Emily McVey, Francesca Metruccio, Martin Paparella, Silvia Pieper, Eugenio Scanziani, Ivana Teodorovic, Paul Van der Brink, Martin Wilks, Keyvin D

title: Expanding Protected Areas to Safeguard Kenya's Herpetofauna Under Climate Change
creator: Ronnie Mwangi Kimani, Chunrong Mi, Patrick Kinyatta Malonza, Beryl A Bwong, Weiguo Du
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Climate change is a major driver of biodiversity loss, particularly for ectothermic species such as reptiles and amphibians (hereafter herpetofauna), which are highly sensitive to environmental changes. While extensive research has evaluated the effectiveness of protected areas (PAs) in conserving biodiversity under climate change in developed and rapidly developing countries, similar studies in Africa remain scarce despite the continent's exceptional biodiversity.

title: Quantum‐Mechanically Refined, Dynamics‐Coupled, and AI‐Augmented Elucidation of Epigenetic Inhibition: An In Silico Paradigm Targeting HDAC8 of Schistosoma mansoni
creator: Mohd Imran, Talha Jawaid, Hayaa M Alhuthali, Amani A Alrehaili, Abdullah R Alzahrani, Zia Ur Rehman, Elliot Mbunge, Tafadzwa Dzinamarira, Wei Wang
description: The increasing burden of schistosomiasis, compounded by the restriction imposed by monotherapeutic regimens, highlights the pressing need for new molecules that target specific molecular pathways. Schistosoma mansoni histone deacetylase 8 (SmHDAC8), a zinc‐dependent epigenetic regulator, has emerged as a nonredundant and druggable enzyme, critical for parasite survival, fertility, and chromatin homeostasis.

title: Chimeric degraders in neurodegenerative diseases: Challenges and future directions
creator: Hanyuan Zheng, Kun Cui, Jian Mao, You Wan, Jie Zheng
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). s, such as small-molecule inhibitors and antibodies, have achieved limited success against these “undruggable” proteins.[3]

In recent years, targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a strategy to eliminate disease-driving proteins by co-opting endogenous disposal systems.[4] These agents, collectively termed targeting chimeras (TACs), are bifunctional molecules that use one warhead to bind the target protein and a second module to recruit a cellular degradation mechanism.

title: Fe-doped MoS2 monolayers for CO, H2S, and NO2 detection: towards advanced environmental sensors
creator: N. V. Hoang, Tr. Q. Trieu
description: In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations integrated with machine learning via the crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) were employed to systematically investigate the electronic, magnetic, thermomechanical, and optical properties of Fe-doped MoS2 (Fe-MoS2) monolayers before and after the adsorption of CO, H2S, and NO2 gas molecules.

title: Apoptosis, Cell Cycle and Differentiation Effects of Propolis Extracted in Olive Oil on HL‐60 AML Cells: A Flow Cytometric Analysis
creator: Hamide Dogan, A Ata Ozcimen, Erkan Alabas, Sibel Silici, Yasemin Saygideger, Birgul Ozdemir, Consuelo Amantini
description: In recent years, researchers have focused on the drug capacity of natural products and their components with low side effects in the treatment of leukemia. This study aims to elucidate the antileukemic mechanism of action of olive oil extract of propolis (OEP) together with methylprednisolone (MP) in HL‐60 cells, an acute myeloid leukemia cell line.

title: Genotype-guided isoniazid dosing harmonizes drug exposure in 3HP tuberculosis preventive therapy
creator: Kesia Esther da Silva, Samuel Sarkodie, Karina Marques, Patricia Vieira, Roberto Dias de Oliveira, Paulo César Pereira dos Santos, Marco Antonio Moreira Puga, Allyson Guimarães Costa, João Paulo Gregorio Machado, Renata Spener-Gomes, Eunsol Yang, Rada Savic, Marcelo Cordeiro-Santos, Julio Croda, Jas
description: RationalePolymorphisms in the N-acetyltransferase 2 (NAT2) gene explain much of the interindividual variation in isoniazid (INH) metabolism and determine risk of toxicities. However, there is limited evidence to guide INH dose adjustment according to the NAT2 acetylator profile in weekly rifapentine-INH tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT).

title: Spatial Mapping of the Lung Cancer Ecosystem Reveals Distinct Patterns of Intratumoral and Internodular Heterogeneity
creator: Bum-Seo Baek, Ki-Hyun Kim, Seung-jae Kim, Jacob D. Eccles, Minhyung Kim, Sungyong You, Christian Ascoli, Gye Young Park
description: The spatial organization of malignant and non-malignant cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME) critically influences tumor evolution and therapeutic response. However, the architecture of micro-niches remains incompletely understood. Leveraging Xenium-based spatial transcriptomics, we comprehensively mapped the spatial ecosystem of an orthotopic murine lung cancer model, identifying distinct spatial domains that form unique, organized cellular neighborhoods.

title: A mechanistic basis for CD8+ T cell expansion sensitivity as a predictor of HIV post-treatment control
creator: Tin Phan, Nicole Pagane, Jasmine Kreig, Aurelien Marc, Macauley Locke, Michael J Peluso, Demi A Sandel, Amelia N Deitchman, Rachel L Rutishauser, Steven G Deeks, Ruian Ke, Ruy M Ribeiro, Alan S Perelson
description: A key goal in HIV-1 cure research is to understand why some individuals control viral rebound after stopping antiretroviral therapy (ART). Recent human studies have identified responding CD8+ T cells expressing Ki-67 and the transcription factor TCF-1 as correlates of post-treatment control, but the mechanistic basis of this association remains unclear.

title: POU2AF2/OCA-T1 coactivates POU2F2 and defines a lineage-specific dependency in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
creator: Rima Tulaiha, Liam Shanley, Amanda Luvisotto, Ping Wang, Vipul Shukla, Zibo Zhao, Feng Yue, Ali Shilatifard, Christopher R Vakoc, Lu Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Lineage-restricted transcriptional programs establish cell identity and can create selective dependencies in cancer. Here, we identify POU2AF2, encoding the transcriptional co-activator OCA-T1, as a critical lineage-specific dependency in a subset of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Pan-cancer dependency analyses and patient cohorts reveal elevated POU2AF2 expression in genetically aggressive DLBCL, where its depletion markedly suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo .

title: Virtual Reality Application for Teaching Complex Congenital Heart Defect Anatomy: Design and Development Study
creator: Kevin Muneton, David Buyck, Carlos-Eduardo Guerrero-Chalela, Shanti Narasimhan, Paul A Iaizzo, Tiffany Leung
description: BackgroundMedical education still faces challenges in teaching complex human cardiac anatomy to a wide range of learners, especially in the subject of congenital heart defects. Traditional educational methods such as cadaver dissection and the use of textbooks still face some limitations, for example, specimen availability and student comfort.

title: Optimal depolarization sequence for cardiac resynchronization therapy patients
creator: Ksenia Sedova, Jan Azarov, Peter M Van Dam, Karol Curila, Pavel Leinveber, Josef Kautzner, Frieder Braunschweig
description: AimsElectrical ventricular dyssynchrony is a hallmark of intraventricular conduction disease in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Although cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is effective, a proportion of patients with electrical dyssynchrony evidenced by an electrocardiogram (ECG) remain non-responders. Besides the QRS duration, visualization and quantification of the depolarization sequence could contribute to improving CRT response.

creator: Unknown
description:
ers and patients with diabetes and prediabetes treated with Xience Sierra everolimus-eluting stents: COASTLINE high-risk, European Heart Journal Open, Volume 5, Issue 6, November 2025, oeaf140, https://doi.org/10.1093/ehjopen/oeaf140

In the originally published version of this manuscript, the number of included all-comers treated with resolute-type ZES in the graphical abstract was incorrectly stated as 1,317. This should instead be 2,416.

This error has been corrected and the graphical abstract resupplied.

title: Zinc diamyldithiocarbamate
creator: Andrea Hartwig, MAK Commission
description: The German Senate Commission for the Investigation of Health Hazards of Chemical Compounds in the Work Area (MAK Commission) has evaluated the data for zinc diamyldithiocarbamate [15337-18-5] to derive an occupational exposure limit value (maximum concentration at the workplace, MAK value) considering all toxicological end points.

title: The use of cold-stored platelets to provide hemostasis in dogs with thrombocytopenia
creator: Shannon A Monaco, Jillian M Haines, Sarah C Guess, Sybil M Fiedler, K Jane Wardrop
description: BackgroundPlatelet transfusion can be lifesaving in dogs with severe thrombocytopenia and hemorrhage, but platelet products are limited by short shelf life and contamination risk. Cold-stored platelets (CSP) may provide a practical alternative, but in vivo hemostatic efficacy in dogs is unknown.Hypothesis/ObjectivesEvaluate the clinical hemostatic efficacy and safety of CSP transfusions in thrombocytopenic dogs.

title: Viral Infection‐Induced Epilepsy and the Gut Microbiome Crosstalk
creator: Xi Guo, Niomi R Kaiser, Susan L Campbell
description: Viral infections of the central nervous system (CNS) pose a significant risk for seizures, and in some cases, long‐term epileptogenesis. Seizure development following viral infection involves diverse CNS mechanisms, with emerging evidence that peripheral factors, including gut microbiome composition and immune‐inflammatory responses, also contribute.

title: Closed-Loop Multi-Objective Optimization for Receptor-Selective Cell-Penetrating Peptide Design
creator: Iori Yamahata, Hidetomo Yokoo, Yosuke Demizu, Teppei Shimamura, Shuto Hayashi
description: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can deliver diverse cargoes into cells. However, designing CPPs with receptor-selective interaction profiles remains difficult because interactions with individual cell-surface components cannot be tuned independently. Here, we developed a closed-loop in silico framework for receptor-selective CPP design, in which receptor interactions are formulated as explicit objectives in a multi-objective optimization problem.

title: What is public health advocacy? Australasian practitioner perspectives on defining the field and identifying effective practice and required competencies
creator: Alexandra J Bhatti, Sophia Lin, Katherine Cullerton, Dannielle Post, Nathan Dawes, Janaki Amin, Josephine Y Chau
description: Public health advocacy is a core function of public health practice, yet it remains underexamined, with limited consensus on its definition, effective strategies, and required competencies. This study explored public health advocacy practice among Australasian advocates, examining how advocacy is defined, which strategies are perceived as effective, and the competencies required for practice.

title: Expression analysis of hsp70 and hsp90 chaperone-encoding genes in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) in response to osmotic stress
creator: Abdul Rahem Faqih, Seto Sugianto Prabowo Rahardjo, Ellana Sanoesi, Septi Anitasari, Diana Aisyah, Cinca Hayyu Putri Satiti, Asad Aulia Iqomuddin, Rahayu Salsabila, Wahyu Surya Prasdiawan
description: Braja 001 Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is a locally developed hybrid strain intended for brackish-water aquaculture in Indonesia. This study evaluated the molecular stress response using hsp70 and hsp90 genes, together with endocrine, hematological, immune, and respiratory indicators, to determine the adaptive capacity of Braja 001 tilapia under different salinity levels.

title: Management of cT2N0M0 esophageal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Yousif Eliya, Samantha Leng, Virginia R Litle, Mohammad Asghari, Geoffrey P Kohn
description: SummaryManagement of cT2N0M0 esophageal cancer is challenging due to staging limitations and limited evidence. While neoadjuvant therapies benefit advanced disease, its role in cT2N0M0 remains unclear, compounded by underrepresentation in trials and the differing responses to treatment between adenocarcinoma (EAC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC).

title: From GROMACS Molecular Dynamics Simulations to Electronic Absorption Spectra: A Tutorial for Small Molecules in Organic Solvents
creator: Chiara Picarelli, Giuseppina Raffaini, Matteo Tommasini
description: Classical molecular dynamics is a theoretical method useful for investigating noncovalent intermolecular interactions and conformational flexibility, enabling the simulation of processes such as aggregation/dissolution and adsorption. Molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry are increasingly introduced in chemistry curricula, yet students may encounter difficulties when translating theoretical concepts into robust simulation protocols, particularly outside biomolecular systems.

title: B-cell receptor signalling and transitional alveolar epithelial cell states in desquamative interstitial pneumonia
creator: Shigeki Saito, Shinya Ohkouchi, Dan Shan, Yasuhiro Kondoh, Ryoko Saito-Koyama, Yong Zhou
description: ExtractDesquamative interstitial pneumonia (DIP), recently termed alveolar macrophage pneumonia in the updated European Respiratory Society/American Thoracic Society classification, is a rare smoking-associated interstitial lung disease (ILD) characterised by diffuse intra-alveolar macrophage accumulation and variable interstitial remodelling [1]. Although macrophage accumulation represents the defining histopathologic feature, the immune pathways and epithelial injury programmes associated with DIP remain poorly characterised.

title: Nonadherence to inhaled corticosteroids is associated with negative mepolizumab response
creator: Mohammed Ghazi Almutairi, John Marriott, Zahraa Jalal, Louise Wood, Samantha Caddick, Babita Rajkumari, Susan Renwick, Siobhan Wilkinson, Caroline Gallagher, Hollie Morgan, Adel H. Mansur
description: BackgroundNonadherence to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in severe asthma is associated with poor control and may impair response to biologics. The primary objective of the present study was to evaluate ICS nonadherence influence on mepolizumab treatment response in adults with severe eosinophilic asthma.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we compared ICS nonadherence rates in mepolizumab responders and nonresponders.

title: UcTCRp: a TCRβ-based framework for identifying and profiling MAIT- and iNKT-associated repertoire signals
creator: Linlin Chen, Yueyi Li, Shiwen Shan, Kaixuan Wang, Chao Feng, Yunsheng Dou, Qihang Xu, Linru Cai, Hao Wang, Haiyang Wang, Xiaochen Bo, Jian Zhang
description: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells and invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells are conventionally identified using invariant or semi-invariant TCRα chains, antigen-loaded tetramers, or transcriptomic phenotypes. These requirements limit their detection in public and clinical immune-repertoire datasets that contain only TCRβ sequences.

title: Experimental and Computational Investigations of Surface Polaritons at Metal‐Oxide‐Semiconductor Interfaces
creator: Humaira Zafar, Qiang Zhang, Rainer Straubinger, Ayman Rezek, Mauro Pereira, Ammar Nayfeh, Dalaver H. Anjum
description: Planar surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) at metal–oxide–semiconductor (MOS) interfaces are central to plasmon‐assisted optoelectronic and tunneling devices, where ultrathin dielectrics govern field confinement and energy transfer. However, a direct link between electron energy‐loss spectroscopy (EELS) measurements and electromagnetic power dissipation at buried interfaces remains unclear.

title: Trigger-based adaptive proton therapy and changes in target coverage and cardiac dose in esophageal cancer
creator: Vlad Badiu, Esther Kneepkens, Dominique Reijtenbagh, Maaike Berbée, Richard Canters
description: Background and purposeInter-fractional anatomical variations during proton therapy for esophageal cancer may compromise target coverage and increase dose to surrounding organs. Adaptive replanning can mitigate these effects, but its cumulative dose-based and clinical impact remains insufficiently characterized. We evaluated offline adaptive intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) triggered by target underdose or cardiac overdose using deformable dose accumulation.

title: Rolling‐Enabled Nonplanar Heterogeneous Integration for Polarization‐Diverse Nanolasers on Silicon Photonics
creator: Byoung Jun Park, Dongmin Shin, Aran Yu, Byeong Uk You, Jaeho Lee, Sang‐Wook Han, Seung‐Woo Jeon, Dongyeon Daniel Kang, Myung‐Ki Kim
description: The continued advancement of silicon photonics increasingly relies on heterogeneous integration beyond monolithic fabrication, with transfer printing emerging as a powerful strategy for deterministic and high‐precision assembly. However, existing transfer‐printing strategies remain fundamentally limited to planar integration, restricting access to orientation‐dependent optical functionalities.

title: Feasibility of longitudinal prostate R2⁎ measurements in patients undergoing stereotactic ablative radiotherapy on an MRI-linac
creator: Chris Moore, Asher Ezekiel, Vodathi Bamunuarachchi, Ereny Saad, Anubhav Datta, Peter Hoskin, Ananya Choudhury, Marcel van Herk, David L. Buckley, Michael J. Dubec, Damien J. McHugh
description: Background and PurposeTissue R2* (1/T2*), sensitive to deoxyhaemoglobin, is a proposed hypoxia biomarker in prostate cancer. This exploratory work investigates prostate R2* and volume throughout and after hypo-fractionated radiotherapy and the effects of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).Materials and methodsFifteen patients (seven with ADT) received five-fraction stereotactic-ablative-radiotherapy (SABR) on a 1.

title: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial
creator: Maria Boldó Alcaine, Maria José Durà Mata, Gabriel-Fernando Sandoval Ruíz, Maria Llaberia Marcual, Marta Carceller de la Torre, Mar Domingo Teixidor, Evelyn Santiago Vacas, Antoni Bayés Genís, Magnus Bäck
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsCardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but access remains suboptimal. Telerehabilitation may overcome barriers, yet evidence from real-world, public health systems is limited. This randomized controlled trial study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured telerehabilitation programme compared with standard centre-based CR in patients after ACS, focussing on cardiovascular risk factor control and lifestyle adherence.Methods and resultsTELECOR is a pragmatic, open-label, randomized trial conducted at a tertiary public hospital.

title: Reconfigurable Terahertz Multi‐Harmonic Dual‐Combs
creator: Xuhong Ma, Zhiwei Qin, Xianglong Bi, Ziping Li, Wenjian Wan, Binbin Liu, Guibin Liu, Yue Pan, Yanming Lu, Hua Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dual‐comb spectroscopy, constructed from two frequency combs with slightly different repetition frequencies, enables real‐time and high‐precision measurements without mechanical scanning. In the terahertz (THz) spectral range, dual‐comb techniques provide a powerful tool for high‐resolution and rapid spectroscopy. Quantum cascade lasers (QCLs), owing to their compact footprint and favorable size, weight, and power (SWaP), have emerged as promising sources for THz dual‐comb systems.

title: So, we are now talking dentistry – And it will indeed be a mouthful
creator: Jasmine Ho
description: rtunity to introduce aspects of dentistry to a predominantly medical readership, with the hope of demystifying dental service provision, education, and the patient experience. Traditionally, OMFS surgeons were dentally qualified first before pursuing medical training to be eligible for OMFS training.

title: Probing Molecular Chirality via Linear Dichroism of Molecule‐Loaded Anisotropic Plasmonic Slots
creator: EunSu Jeon, YoonYeong Ko, Seungwoo Choi, SeokJae Yoo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Conventional chiroptical spectroscopy relies on circularly polarized light (CPL), yet inherent retardance errors in CPL generation compromise signal fidelity and introduce artifacts from crosstalk with linear dichroism and birefringence. Here, we theoretically propose Chiroptical sensing via Linear dichroism of Anisotropic Plasmonic Slots (CLAPS), a CPL‐free chiroptical sensing scheme that employs two linearly polarized light (LPL) beams tilted with respect to the orientation axis of a plasmonic slot array filled with chiral analytes.

title: DeepU-PRS: nonlinear and uncertainty-aware SNP heritability modeling for annotation-informed polygenic risk scoring
creator: Junhyeong Lee, Dokyoon Kim, Seunggeun Lee
description: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) are widely used to quantify genetic predisposition to complex traits, and their predictive accuracy can be enhanced by incorporating functional annotations into single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) effect-size estimation. Existing approaches typically assume linear relationships between annotations and SNP effects, neglecting predictive aleatoric variance and potential nonlinear regulatory interactions.

title: Pancreatic hydatid cyst with a characteristic “water-lily” sign
creator: Aminreza Abkhoo, Niloufar Ayoobi, Seyed Mohammad Amin Dashti, Faeze Salahshour
description: BackgroundCystic echinococcosis rarely involves the pancreas and may mimic common cystic neoplasms. Recognition of characteristic imaging signs is central to diagnosis; the “water-lily” sign (floating detached endocyst) is a rare and highly characteristic finding in favor of transitional-stage hydatid cyst and, when recognized, can prevent inappropriate cyst puncture and guide stage- and anatomy-based management.

title: Mapping the frontiers of genomic disease surveillance research in the ASEAN region: scientometric insights for precision public health and next-generation epidemic intelligence
creator: Jerico Bautista Ogaya, Rahmatullah Nazari, Olalekan John Okesanya, Andres Phillip Mayol, Emmanueal M Cabanig, Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed, Murtaza Jafari, Roel Nickelson M Solano, Joey Salinas Ramos, Zhinya Kawa Othman, Adriana Viola Miranda, Shuaibu Saidu Musa, Mae Frances G Sanico, Rolando A Alimen, Lin
description: Genomic disease surveillance has become a cornerstone of precision public health, yet the regional research architecture in Southeast Asia remains insufficiently characterized. This study provides a comprehensive scientometric mapping of genomic surveillance research in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region and identifies patterns relevant to the development of epidemic intelligence systems.

title: Correction to: DeepDrugs: a mechanism-aware tri-linear attention framework for synergistic drug-combination prediction
creator: Unknown
description:
ipt, the affiliation for co-author Hua Wang erroneously read “Department of Neurosurgery, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University, Jinan 250021, China”.

This has been corrected to read “Department of Neurology, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University, Jinan 250021, China”.

title: The near extinction of the RAPTOR: a cautionary tale
creator: Andrew W Kirkpatrick, Eric Herget, Shane Smith, Paul B McBeth, Paul Duffy, Mark Nutley, Chad G Ball
description: SummaryTrauma hybrid operating rooms (THORs) integrate diagnostic imaging with open surgical capabilities to provide both surgical and interventional radiology procedures, such as may be required by exsanguinating patients, in a single physical location. The world’s first trauma program–designed THOR, designated the Resuscitation with Angiography, Percutaneous Treatments, and Operative Repair (RAPTOR) suite, opened in Calgary in 2013.

title: The THAW protocol: A zero-cost traditional biomechanical adjunct to enhance clinical Nasya practices
creator: Ram Rahim GSI MSG, Puneet Maheshwari
description: dizing Marsha Nasya (MN), a vital Panchakarma therapy. We were particularly struck by the panel's consensus on preparatory procedures (Purvakarma), such as sudation (Sweda), and the emphasis on the need for people-centered frameworks to ensure equitable access to Ayurvedic therapies [1].

title: Minimally invasive Ayurveda management of recurrent and acute-on-chronic non-healing venous leg ulceration – a Case Report
creator: AS Santhi Krishna, Sujith Eranezhath, Arun T Namboothiri
description: Slow healing and recurrent venous leg ulcers resulting from varicose veins due to lower limb chronic venous insufficiency are common vascular complications. If left untreated, they may lead to severe outcomes such as hemorrhage and, in extreme cases, limb amputation.

title: A Comprehensive Toolkit to Support Self‐Report Questionnaires for Autistic Adults With Cognitive Disability
creator: Vicky Caron, Isabelle Courcy, Isabelle Soulières
description: ObjectivesAutistic individuals with cognitive disability are underrepresented in research using self‐report measures. This study aimed to develop a toolkit of customizable accommodations to facilitate self‐report and to explore its usability through implementation with quality of life (QoL) questionnaires.MethodsA consultation process in three rounds was conducted with 10 experts in autism and/or cognitive disability to identify accommodations.

title: Transition from paediatric to adult congenital heart disease care in Central and South-Eastern Europe: current practices and opportunities for improvement
creator: Alexandra Arvanitaki, Katja Prokšelj, Iveta Šimkova, Irena Ivanac Vranešić, Agnese Strenge, Monika Komar, Magdalena Lipczynska, Anna Kaneva, Lina Gumbiene, Petra Antonova, Hajnalka Olga Balint, Ioan Mircea Coman, Umit Yasar Sinan, Maryanne Caruana, Aleksandra Nikolic, Maarja Maser, Elena Panfile, Ma
description: AimsTransition from paediatric to adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) care is a critical determinant of lifelong disease management for individuals with congenital heart disease (CHD). However, structured transition programmes remain inconsistently implemented, and data are lacking on current practices in Central and South-Eastern European (CESEE) countries.

title: Orbital hematoma following ruthenium-106 plaque brachytherapy: Potential dosimetric implications
creator: Efstathios T. Detorakis, George Chondrozoumakis, Georgia Solomou, Theocharis Detorakis, Kostas Perisinakis
description: We present a case of a 65-year-old female with choroidal melanoma, who developed an orbital hematoma following ruthenium-106 (106Ru) plaque implantation. The patient, with a history of recurrent ipsilateral subconjunctival hemorrhages and arterial hypertension, experienced intense coughing immediately following the completion of surgery and extubation. Subsequently, she developed an orbital hematoma (confirmed by B-scan ultrasonography).

title: Cardiovascular Health and Cognitive Function in Early Midlife: A Cross‐Sectional Analysis of the 1970 British Cohort Study
creator: Scott T Chiesa, Sarah‐Naomi James, Alun D Hughes
description: BackgroundPoor cardiovascular health in midlife increases risk of dementia in later years. At least some of this risk may stem from early decrements in cognitive ability in those with poor cardiovascular health that are already evident by midlife. Whether such associations are causal, however, or develop in tandem due to shared factors encountered earlier in life, remains unclear.

title: Exploring Peripheral Blood Biomarkers for Dementia Diagnosis in Latin American Populations
creator: Ariel Caviedes, Paulina Orellana, Hernan Hernandez, Andrea Slachevsky, María Isabel Behrens, Diana Matallana, Francisco Lopera, Nilton Custodio, Martin Alejandro Bruno, José Alberto Avila Funes, Leonel Tadao Takada, Stefanie D Pina‐Escudero, Victor Valcour, Kenneth S Kosik, Bruce L Miller, Jennifer
description: BackgroundDementia, encompassing Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), poses a substantial public health challenge in Latin America. Barriers such as a shortage of healthcare professionals, limited medical accessibility, and underdiagnosis contribute to the complexity. While biomarkers aligned with the ATN framework (Amyloid, Tau, Neurodegeneration) have revolutionized diagnosis, their cost limits adoption in Latin America.

title: Prognostic Significance of Serum Sodium in Patients With Acute Pulmonary Embolism
creator: Patchara Kochaiyapatana, Sukrisd Koowattanatianchai, Jayanton Patumanond, Arwarit Pocathikorn, Sopida Thammongkolchai
description: BackgroundHyponatremia has been associated with adverse outcomes in several cardiovascular diseases; however, its independent prognostic value in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (APE) remains uncertain.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of 105 hospitalized patients with confirmed APE between January 2020 and June 2025. Baseline clinical characteristics were compared between 1-year survivors and non-survivors.

title: Short‐term Sirolimus Treatment Restores Hippocampus and Caudate Volumes and Global Cerebral Blood Flow in Asymptomatic APOE4 Carriers Compared with Non‐carriers
creator: Abeoseh Flemister, Xin Xing, Jessica Overschmidt, Joanne Cassani, Stefan J. Green, David Q. Beversdorf, Carter Woods, John W. Grinstead, Talissa A. Altes, Ai‐Ling Lin, Maalavika Govindarajan
description: BackgroundApolipoprotein ε4 allele (APOE4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for late‐onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Compared with non‐carriers, cognitively normal APOE4 individuals have shown brain atrophy and lower cerebral blood flow (CBF) decades before AD pathological and clinical symptoms appear.

title: Significant Associations of Achilles Tendon Thickness With Atherosclerotic Diseases and Atherosclerotic Risk Factors in Non-Familial Hypercholesterolemia Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Mariko Hakoshima, Hidekatsu Yanai, Tatsuki Onomura, Hirohumi Sugimoto, Hisayuki Katsuyama
description: BackgroundAchilles tendon thickness (ATT) is an important diagnostic tool for familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), a highly atherogenic genetic disorder. Although the available evidence remains limited, recent studies have reported associations between ATT and atherosclerotic diseases and their risk factors among non-FH patients.

title: Neuroinflammation and synaptic markers relate to trajectories of core biomarkers in Alzheimer’s Disease continuum
creator: Ersin Ersoezlue, Julian Hellmann‐Regen, Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMechanisms of cellular senescence affecting neuroimmune responses, homeostasis, and synaptic functioning associate with core Alzheimer’s disease (AD) biomarkers, i.e., pathological aggregation of β‐amyloid (Aβ) and tau protein, while their longitudinal associations remain unclear.MethodThe study cohort included participants from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative study, which consisted of n=65 healthy controls (HC, mean years of every follow‐up visit 4±3), n=41 suspected non‐AD pathology (SNAP, mean years of every follow‐up visit 4±3), and n=198 AD continuum (ADC, mean years of every follow‐up visit 3±3)

title: BRIDGE-KO: auditable transfer learning with bridged knockoffs improves cross-cohort microbiome prediction of immunotherapy response
creator: Jie Sun, Zhenjiang Fan, Rebecca Caldino Bohn, Soyeon Kim, Hyun Jung Park
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transfer learning promises to reuse AI models across biomedical studies, but it often fails when differences between datasets introduce cohort-specific artifacts and ‘negative transfer.’ We present BRIDGE-KO, an interpretable deep-learning framework that turns transfer learning into a testable design process by asking: where to transfer from (source-target coverage and proximity), what to transfer (which representation level is most portable), and how to harmonize data to reduce technical confounding.

title: Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness
creator: Yasemin Derya Gülseren, Derya Aydın, Alev Çetin Duran
description: ObjectiveInfluenza-like illness (ILI) is a major cause of hospitalization during respiratory virus seasons. This study aimed to investigate the pathogens detected in patients presenting with ILI symptoms and to analyze the results in conjunction with clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings.

title: Analyzing Response Rates and Respondent Demographics in Online Surveys Assessing Public Perception of Alzheimer’s Disease‐Modifying Therapies
creator: Saki Nakashima, Kenichiro Sato, Yoshiki Niimi, Tatsushi Toda, Takeshi Iwatsubo
description: BackgroundWith the recent approval of lecanemab, a disease‐modifying therapy (DMT) for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), there is an urgent need to address healthcare system challenges to ensure the safe, effective, and sustainable delivery of approved DMT drugs.Understanding public perceptions of these challenges through online surveys might be helpful.

title: The Strengthening, engaging, and empowering dyads through nutrition & wellness study: a dyadic community‐based nutrition intervention for older adults with diabetes and cognitive impairment
creator: Mirnova E Ceide, Samantha Johnson, Ruchika Darapaneni, Jessica L Zwerling
description: BackgroundA meta‐analysis of over 2.3 million individuals in 14 studies showed that individuals with type II diabetes (T2DM) are at a 60% increased risk for development of any dementia compared to those without T2DM. A Whole Food, Plant Based dietary (WFPB) pattern has been associated with lower blood glucose levels and decreased insulin requirements.

title: Sociodemographic characteristics of nurses entering and leaving the US nursing workforce in 2018 and 2022
creator: Kyla F Woodward, Sue Skillman, Bianca K Frogner
description: IntroductionRegistered nurse (RN) workforce planning relies on a robust understanding of trends in nursing job dynamics. Relevant, current data on RNs' education, training, and job outcomes are critical to implementing solutions to mitigate high job vacancy rates or workforce shortages.

title: Assessing Clinical Research Barriers to the Participation of Underrepresented Groups in the AHEAD Study
creator: Taryn T. James, Carey E. Gleason, Diane Carol Gooding, Fabu P. Carter, Cecilia A. Cardenas, Olivia Deering, Aleshia Cole, Kate Cronin, Cynthia M. Carlsson, Shenikqua Bouges
description: BackgroundTo increase participation of underrepresented groups (URG) into clinical research studies such as the AHEAD study, a study assessing lecanemab in participants with preclinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD), it is necessary to understand and address barriers in an effort to mitigate them. Toward this goal, methods assessing community needs and plans to meet those needs are imperative.

title: Endoscopic accessibility and conduit passage after retrosternal vs. posterior mediastinal gastric conduit reconstruction following McKeown esophagectomy: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Yiming Yao, Dong Jiang, Yifan Shi
description: BackgroundThe optimal route for gastric-conduit reconstruction after McKeown esophagectomy remains uncertain. Previous comparisons have focused primarily on anastomotic leakage and pulmonary morbidity, whereas postoperative endoscopic accessibility and clinically evident conduit-passage disturbance have been less well characterized. We compared retrosternal (RS) and posterior mediastinal (PM) reconstruction, focusing on these functional outcomes.

title: Impact of race/ethnicity and area deprivation index on Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders biomarkers in the POINTER Cohort
creator: Jon B Toledo, Belen Pascual, Susan M Landau, Theresa M Harrison, Quentin Finn, Yitbarek N Demesie, Melissa Yu, Charles Decarli, Prashanthi Vemuri, Laura D Baker, Laura Lovato, Heather M Snyder, Joseph C Masdeu, Valory Pavlik
description: BackgroundThere is limited information on biomarker‐defined Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology in community‐recruited individuals of diverse racial and ethnic groups. Here, we assessed the association of race/ethnicity with baseline biomarkers and cognitive measures and hypothesized a lower impact of AD pathology in non‐Hispanic White (nHW) participants in the U.S.

title: Nonlinear and Vessel-Specific Association Between Coronary Artery Calcium Burden and Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography Underestimation of Coronary Stenosis
creator: Xuzhe Wang, Chengzhuo Wang, Yu Xie, Wenyu Wang, Ruifeng Liu
description: Background:Coronary artery calcium (CAC) introduces substantial artifacts in coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Although calcification is classically associated with overestimation of stenosis severity, underestimation may be even more clinically hazardous because underestimation can lead to inappropriate deferral of revascularization. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the association between CAC burden and CCTA underestimation, with emphasis on vessel-specific anatomical heterogeneity.

title: Brain metabolic subtypes in Long Covid individuals from a Brazilian cohort
creator: Arthur Viana Jotz, Marco De Bastiani, Luiza Santos Machado, Thomas Hugentobler Schlickmann, Maiele Dornelles Silveira, Joana Emilia Senger, Wyllians Vendramini Borelli, João Pedro Ferrari‐Souza, Guilherme Povala, Ana Paula Bornes da Silva, João Pedro Uglione da Ros, Guilherme Bastos de Mello, Matheu
description: BackgroundThe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19), caused by SARS‐CoV‐2, is one of the biggest health concerns of the century. Long COVID is one of the major sequelae from the infection and include persistent neurological manifestations. Brain images study suggest that Long COVID patients present distinct brain metabolic alterations. However, whether brain subtypes of Long COVID exist remains unclear.

title: Management of breakthrough cancer pain in the emergency department
creator: Shin Ahn
description: erant. Accurate assessment of the pain mechanism and opioid status is essential for achieving adequate pain control. MANAGEMENT OF ADULT CANCER PAIN The World Health Organization analgesic ladder remains the cornerstone of cancer pain management. It classifies pain as mild, moderate, or severe and recommends analgesic escalation according to pain intensity.

title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Proteomics in Down Syndrome Identifies Common and Unique Pathological Changes Compared to Late‐Onset and Autosomal Dominant Alzheimer’s Disease
creator: Shijia Bian, Laia Montoliu‐Gaya, Eric B. Dammer, Mathias Sauer, Daniel Alcolea, Kaj Blennow, Henrik Zetterberg, Juan Fortea, Erik C.B. Johnson
description: BackgroundNearly all people with Down Syndrome (DS) develop Alzheimer’s dementia (AD) by the 7th decade of life. However, whether the alterations in fluid biomarker levels associated with DS follow the same pattern to those observed in other forms of AD is not well understood.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Plasma Biomarkers for A/T/N Image Classification in Alzheimer's disease
creator: Han‐Kyeol Kim, Jae Hoon Lee, Joong‐Hyun Chun, Jeong‐Ha Lee, Tim West, Kristopher M Kirmess, Philip B Verghese, Joel B Braunstein, Daniel Connell, Young Hoon Ryu, Chul Hyoung Lyoo, Hanna Cho
description: BackgroundWe aimed to validate the ability of Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers to predict clinical diagnosis and the ability to predict image‐based A/T/N biomarkers positivity in Asian population. We also sought to define the optimal cut point for each biomarker.Method232 participants were enrolled, all of whom underwent 18F‐florbetaben (FBB), 18F‐flortaucipir (FTP) PET, volumetric MRI, and neuropsychological assessments.

title: Gender Differences in the Predictive Efficacy of Mayo‐PACC for Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers: Results from a South American Cohort
creator: Greta Keller, Patricio Chrem Mendez, Nicolas Corvalan, Giulia Solange Clas, María Florencia Álvarez, Lucia Pertierra, Ricardo Allegri, Gustavo Sevlever, Lucia Crivelli, Ezequiel Ignacio Surace
description: BackgroundWith the increase in life expectancy and the rising prevalence of Alzheimer's Disease (AD), the integration of biomarkers for early diagnosis is crucial. The Mayo Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (Mayo‐PACC), encompassing the Rey‐Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT), Trail Making Test ‐ B (TMT B), and semantic fluency, is designed to detect cognitive changes in preclinical AD.

title: Genetic ablation of the adult Leydig cell lineage reveals stem Leydig cells and a peritubular regenerative niche in mice
creator: Laurie Boudreau, Nicholas M Robert, Jacques J Tremblay
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Differentiated Leydig cells (LCs) produce testosterone and INSL3, 2 hormones essential for male sex differentiation and fertility. In mice, the developmental origin of adult Leydig cells (ALCs) and the presence of stem Leydig cells (SLCs) in adulthood remain unresolved. To investigate this, we used the Leydig cell-specific Insl3iCre line combined with Rosa26lox-STOP-lox-iDTR/lox-STOP-lox-TdTomato to genetically ablate the committed LC lineage in adult mice. These mice displayed a normal phenotype without diphtheria toxin (DT).

title: Housing characteristics by living arrangement of older adults with cognitive impairment in the United States
creator: Safiyyah Okoye, Laura N Gitlin
description: BackgroundThe home environment is where daily activities are performed and older adults with and without cognitive impairment spend most of their time. While home safety is a priority for healthcare providers, there is limited understanding of housing characteristics of older adults with cognitive impairment in the United States and whether they differ for those who live alone or with others.

title: Antiplatelet effect of spironolactone via modulation of cPLA2-mediated thromboxane A2 generation in murine platelets
creator: Sanggu Kim, Preeti Kumari Chaudhary, Seongmo Yang, Soochong Kim
description: ImportanceSpironolactone, a steroidal aldosterone antagonist, is widely used as a diuretic and antihypertensive agent. Steroids have been known to promote thrombosis by directly increasing platelet count and activation and indirectly by increasing oxidative stress and suppressing nitric oxide synthesis. However, the effects of spironolactone on platelet activation remain unclear.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging‐negative cerebral amyloid angiopathy: cerebrospinal fluid amyloid‐β42 over amyloid positron emission tomography
creator: Jung‐Min Pyun, Min Ju Kang, Seung Jin Baek, Kyungbok Lee, Young Ho Park, SangYun Kim
description: BackgroundCerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) pathology is becoming increasingly important in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) because of its potential link to amyloid‐related imaging abnormalities, a critical side effect observed during AD immunotherapy. Identification of CAA without typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) markers (MRI‐negative CAA) is challenging, and novel detection biomarkers are needed.

title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Modifies the Association of Cerebral Pulsatility on CSF Biomarkers Related to Neurodegeneration, Synaptic Dysfunction, and Neuroinflammation
creator: Talia L Brach, Brianne M Breidenbach, Matthew P Glittenberg, Leah E Symanski, Tarun Naren, Ira Driscoll, Sarah R Lose, Catherine L Gallagher, Sterling C Johnson, Sanjay Asthana, Tobey J Betthauser, Leonardo A Rivera‐Rivera, Bruce P Hermann, Mark A Sager, Kaj Blennow, Henrik Zetterberg, Cynthia M Car
description: BackgroundCerebral pulsatility (PI) is reportedly higher in individuals with AD and MCI compared to age matched controls and has been associated with greater beta‐amyloid (Aß) burden, but its relationship to other neurodegenerative biomarkers is unknown. Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) positively affects vascular function and is associated with lower PI in several large cerebral vessels.

title: Emergency Department Clinicians’ Needs for User-Centered Antibiotic Guideline: Insights from a Focus Group Interview
creator: Heejeong Kwon, Heun Choi, Soyoon Hwang, Ki Tae Kwon, Song Mi Moon, Myung Jin Lee, Raeseok Lee, Se Yoon Park, Yong Chan Kim, Bongyoung Kim
description: BackgroundInstitution-specific antibiotic guidelines are core components of effective antibiotic stewardship programs; however, their practical use in emergency departments (EDs), where empirical antibiotic decisions are made under time pressure and diagnostic uncertainty, remains limited. This study explored ED clinicians’ perspectives on antibiotic prescribing and identified key elements for developing ED-specific antibiotic guidelines.

title: Differential whole‐brain patterns of cardiometabolic risk and blood biomarker using multi‐modal neuroimaging and explainable deep learning
creator: Da Ma, Samuel N. Lockhart, Timothy M. Hughes, James R. Bateman, Thomas C. Register, Michelle M. Mielke, Metin Nafi Gurcan, Suzanne Craft
description: BackgroundCardiometabolic disorders are emerging risk factors for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD‐related dementia (ADRD). There is currently insufficient understanding of how different cardiometabolic profiles and blood biomarkers impact different AD‐related brain pathology regionally. This project uses data‐driven approaches and explainable artificial intelligence methods to determine the cardiometabolic and fluid contributions toward AD‐related pathophysiologic patterns in the brain.

title: The Impact of a Hand Hygiene Education Program in Long-Term Care Facilities in Korea
creator: Dong Hoon Shin, Rina Lee, Hanju Kim, Sohee Oh, Hyemin Jung, Won Mo Jang, Kyoung Jun Song
description: BackgroundKorea’s rapid population aging has increased demand for long-term care facilities (LTCFs). Because LTCFs are vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks, consistent hand hygiene (HH) practices among caregivers are essential. We evaluated an LTCF-tailored HH education program with measurement of caregiver compliance.

title: Cell cycle-dependent chromatin motion: a role for DNA content doubling over cohesion
creator: Martin Rey-Millet, Léa Costes, Erwan Le Floch, Habib Ayoub, Quentin Saccomani, Manoel Manghi, Kerstin Bystricky
description: The spatiotemporal organization of chromatin in the eukaryotic nucleus is fundamental for genome regulation. Chromatin undergoes rapid remodelling and rearrangements within minutes, altering its diffusion properties. Considering the tight coupling between genome function and nuclear architecture, a key question is how chromatin dynamics adapt to or promote nuclear processes.

title: Circulating stress hormones and multimodal measures of brain and cognition in older adults: Cross‐sectional findings from the AGE‐WELL cohort
creator: Maxie Liebscher, Silke White, Edelweiss Touron, Florence Mézenge, Anne Chocat, Laurent Coulbaut, Denis Vivien, Vincent De la Sayette, Natalie L Marchant, Gael Chételat, Olga M Klimecki, Géraldine Poisnel, Miranka Wirth, Medit‐Ageing Research Group
description: BackgroundIncreased stress, a proposed risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), is associated with increased brain and cognitive vulnerabilities in older populations, which may be different in women and men.ObjectiveTo examine cross‐sectional associations between circulating stress hormones (epinephrine, norepinephrine, cortisol, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS), and DHEAS/cortisol ratio) and multimodal measures of brain health and cognition sensitive to AD.

title: Community-based solutions: a principles-to-practice framework to support individuals living with dementia and their care partners
creator: Allie Peckham, Monika Roerig, Sage Sadow, Frances Morton-Chang, Laura Schmid, Clare Schuchardt, Molly Budhiraja, Sara Allin
description: Background and ObjectivesAlzheimer’s disease and related dementias represent a global public health concern, with persistent gaps in supports for individuals living with dementia and their unpaid care partners. This study synthesized promising community-based innovations that address these gaps and contribute to positive outcomes.

title: Alzheimer disease incidence increases with country‐level intake of Omega‐6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids
creator: Timothy H Ciesielski, Razaq O Durodoye, Giuseppe Tosto, Margaret A Pericak‐Vance, Jonathan L Haines, Alzheimer’s Disease Genetics Consortium (ADGC), Scott M Williams
description: BackgroundEvidence from diverse fields implicates lipid dysfunction in Alzheimer Disease (AD) pathogenesis. However, lipid consumption at the individual level does not vary greatly within most study cohorts, and multiple lipids are rarely well‐measured concurrently. In contrast, mean lipid intakes at the country‐level can be precisely estimated and can vary substantially across countries.

title: Predicting Future Conversion from Amyloid‐β Negativity to Positivity: Time‐To‐Event Prediction with Machine Learning
creator: Amirali Vahid, Jafar Zamani, Hadi Hosseini
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the gradual accumulation of amyloid‐β (Aβ) plaques and tau tangle pathologies in the brain. Extant studies highlight that Aβ deposition contributes significantly to tau accumulation, leading to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Individuals with positive Aβ are more susceptible to AD progression but the precise spatial and temporal pattern of Aβ leading to convergence from negative to positive status is unclear.

title: Genome-Wide Risk Assessment and Clinical Prediction of Iodinated Contrast Media–Induced Anaphylaxis
creator: Soo Jie Chung, Eunsoon Shin, Yong-Seok Kim, So-Hee Lee, Sun-Sin Kim, Sun Young Paik, Heung-woo Park, Sae-Hoon Kim, Sungwon Jeon, Jong Bhak, Hye-Ryun Kang, Yoon-Seok Chang
description: PurposeIodinated contrast media (ICM) are widely used in diagnostic imaging, but may trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. Although human leukocyte antigen (HLA) associations have been proposed, genome-wide evidence remains limited. To identify genetic risk variants associated with ICM-induced anaphylaxis and evaluate their clinical utility.

title: Unsupervised online reaction time test improves estimation of cognitive function in a large sample of cognitively‐asymptomatic older adults
creator: Xinyi Wang, Aidan Bindoff, Rebecca J St George, Eddy Roccati, Larissa Bartlett, Katherine Lawler, Alastair J Noyce, Son Tran, Anna E King, James C Vickers, Quan Bai, Jane E Alty
description: BackgroundFinding low‐cost, accessible methods to detect people at risk of preclinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a research priority for neuroprotective drug development and clinical trials. Sub‐clinical asymptomatic decline in episodic memory is a proxy measure of preclinical AD and there is emerging evidence that analysis of motor patterns using laboratory apparatus may detect this stage.

title: Impacts and Immune Mechanisms of Pollutant-Mediated Asthma and Airway Inflammation
creator: Sang-Min Yoon, Min-Hyeok An, Pureun-Haneul Lee, An-Soo Jang
description: Air pollution is a major environmental risk factor contributing to the development, exacerbation, and persistence of asthma. A wide range of airborne pollutants, including particulate matter (PM), ozone (O3), nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, diesel exhaust particles (DEPs), volatile organic compounds, and biological contaminants, can interact with the airway epithelium and immune system, leading to dysregulated inflammatory responses.

title: Contrast‐agnostic deep‐learning‐based detection of perivascular spaces in magnetic resonance imaging
creator: Mario Díaz, Erelle Fuchs, Hendrik Mattern, Daniel Behme, Roberto Duarte, Maria del C. Valdes Hernandez, Joanna M Wardlaw, Stefanie Schreiber, Maria Trujillo, Jose Bernal Moyano
description: BackgroundTo date, all computerised perivascular spaces (PVS) quantification methods require case‐wise, imaging modality, or study‐specific parameter adjustments, and suffer from generalisability problems in clinical settings, and misdetection of other cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) markers. We propose a deep learning‐based PVS detection method to overcome these issues.

title: Unraveling the Molecular Heterogeneity of Asthma Through Blood Transcriptomics
creator: Soyoon Sim, Byungju Min, Hae-Sim Park
description: ptoms and contributing to disease severity.1,2 Thus, the management of severe asthma has increasingly centered on biologic therapies targeting immunoglobulin E (IgE), interleukin (IL)-4/-13, IL-5, and thymic stromal lymphopoietin, with surrogate markers, such as high blood eosinophil counts (BECs) and fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), being used to identify patients with T2-high phenotypes.

title: Efficient enzyme-mediated degradation of various emerging pollutants, including 2-mercaptobenzothiazole, paracetamol, and sulfamethoxazole, using HRP@UiO-66-NH2
creator: Khadega A. Al-Maqdi, Shaikha Alneyadi, Nada Elmerhi, Lamia A. Siddig, Ahmed Alzamly, Iltaf Shah, Syed Salman Ashraf
description: The increasing contamination of water sources due to industrialization and population growth poses significant environmental and health risks, even at trace pollutant concentrations. Enzymatic bioremediation, particularly using horseradish peroxidase (HRP), has shown great potential in pollutant degradation due to its high selectivity and catalytic efficiency. However, limitations such as poor operational stability and reusability hinder its large-scale application.

title: Metabolomics approaches for capturing the chemical exposome and its influences on cognitive function and brain health
creator: M Arthur Moseley, Oliver Fiehn, Pieter Dorrestein, Tuulia Hyotylainen, Matej Oresic, David Wishart, Nina Zhao, Rima F Kaddurah‐Daouk, Alzheimer's Gut Microbiome Project Consortium (AGMP)
description: BackgroundThere is growing interest in the role of environmental factors (i.e., exposome) in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s diseases.
