title: Optimal transport for label transfer in single-cell multi-omics integration
creator: Junjun Ren, Zhengqian Zhang, Jiayu Wang, Lingyun Xie, Jialiang Wang, Meng Wang, Yongzhuang Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Single-cell multi-omics datasets are rapidly expanding, and integrating complementary modalities can provide a more comprehensive view of the molecular mechanisms underlying biological processes. However, cross-modality alignment remains challenging due to modality-specific measurement differences and mismatches in cell-type proportions. Here, we present single-cell Optimal Transport-based Label Transfer (scOT-LT), a semi-supervised label-transfer framework that aligns single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and scATAC-seq data using label-aware unbalanced optimal transport, which tolerates compositional mismatch while favoring label-consistent correspondences.

title: Hyperspectral TERS Imaging Reveals Strain Heterogeneity in Individual Nanoplastic Particles
creator: Anushree Dutta, Siiri Bienz, Naresh Kumar, Renato Zenobi
description: Nanoplastics pose growing environmental and health risks, yet their label-free, nondestructive detection and characterization, especially at the single-particle level, remain challenging. Here, we deploy AFM-based tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (AFM-TERS) to chemically characterize individual polystyrene (PS) nanoplastic particles via hyperspectral imaging under ambient conditions.

title: Peptide Toxins from Marine Conus Snails with Activity on Potassium Channels and/or Currents
creator: Luis Martínez-Hernández, Estuardo López-Vera, Manuel B. Aguilar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Toxins from Conus snails are peptides characterized by a great structural and functional diversity. They have a high affinity for a wide range of membrane proteins such as ion channels, neurotransmitter transporters, and G protein-coupled receptors.

title: 1990–2021年糖尿病肾病的全球、区域及国家和地区负担分析
creator: 雅娴 宁, 小春 周, 勾琴 王, 丽丽 张, 俭勤 王
description: 目的基于全球疾病负担（Global Burden of Diseases, GBD）2021数据，系统分析了1990–2021年全球204个国家和地区糖尿病肾病（diabetic kidney disease, DKD）的疾病负担趋势及未来十年预测。方法GBD 1990–2021年DKD数据，采用年龄标准化率（age-standardized rates, ASRs）和平均年度百分比变化（average annual percentage change, AAPC）分析趋势，运用联结点回归模型（Joinpoint regression model, JRM）识别转折点，自回归积分移动平均模型（autoregressive integrated moving average, ARIMA）预测未来趋势，R软件实现统计分析。结果1990–2021年全球DKD年龄标准化发病率（age-standardized incidence rate, ASIR）、年龄标准化死亡率（age-standardized death rate, ASDR）呈显著上升，累计分别上升55.0%〔95%置信区间（confidence interval, CI）：42.3%～69.8%，P<0.001〕、57.3%（95%CI：43.1%～73.5%，P<0.001）；年龄标准化患病率（age-standardized prevalence rate, ASPR）累计下降37.5%（95%CI：－45.2%～－28.8%，P<0.001）；年龄标准化伤残调整寿命年（age-standardized disability-adjusted life years, DALYs）率累计上升56.2%（95%CI：42.8%～71.5%，P<0.001）。国家和地区间负担差异显著，格陵兰ASPR上升幅度最大，英国ASPR降幅最大；爱沙尼亚ASIR增幅最高，爱尔兰ASIR降幅最大；美国ASDR上升最显著，马尔代夫ASDR下降最明显。东亚现患病例数最多，南亚新发病例与DALYs负担最重，低社会人口指数（socio-demographic index, SDI）地区上升更显著。未来十年（2022–2031年）预测显示，全球DKD ASPR年均上升0.45%（95%CI：0.21%～0.69%），ASIR年均下降0.23%（95%CI：－0.47%～－0.01%），年龄标准化DALYs率年均上升1.12%（95%CI：0.89%～1.35%），疾病总负担仍将持续加重。结论全球DKD疾病负担日益加重，低SDI地区尤为显著，亟需在高负担区域采取精准防控措施，为公共卫生资源配置提供科学依据。 糖尿病肾病（diabetic kidney disease, DKD）是以蛋白尿和肾功能下降为主要特征的糖尿病微血管并发症，可进展至终末期肾病（end-stage renal disease, ESRD）[1]。2021年全球糖尿病患者已达8.4亿，其中DKD患者人数超3.

title: Repurposing of the antimalarial agent tafenoquine to combat MRSA
creator: Pengfei She, Yifan Yang, Linhui Li, Yimin Li, Shasha Liu, Zehao Li, Linying Zhou, Yong Wu
description: Staphylococcus aureus is an important human pathogen that often leads to hospital-acquired and community-acquired infections. The appearance of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) has made the treatment extremely challenging. There is an urgent need to develop new antimicrobial agents to combat MRSA infections.

title: Use of pimobendan in cats: a practical evidence-based review
creator: Sonya G Gordon, Ashley B Saunders, Sonya Wesselowski, Elizabeth L Malcolm, Alice Watson
description: Practical relevance:Cardiomyopathies are a common condition and the leading cause of congestive heart failure (CHF) in cats; however, to date there have been limited therapeutic options available. Commonly used therapeutics include diuretics for CHF and antithrombotics 2 to reduce the risk of arterial thromboembolism (ATE), which do not directly affect myocardial function.

title: A Consensus‐Based Glossary for Controversial Terminology in Root and Canal Anatomy
creator: Hany Mohamed Aly Ahmed, Venkateshbabu Nagendrababu, Ali Keleş, Thomas Gerhard Wolf, Henry F. Duncan, Ove Andreas Peters, Paul Michael Howell Dummer, Abhishek Parolia, Abhishek Parolia, Alfredo Sierra‐Cristancho, Andrea Lisa Waber, Antonis Chaniotis, Azhar Iqbal, Blaine Murray Cleghorn, Cangül Keskin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimTo produce a glossary of controversial terminology relating to a variety of anatomical features of root canals.Materials and MethodsA multi‐stage consensus process was designed and applied to generate definitions for controversial terms describing root and canal anatomy. The overall direction of the project was provided by an Executive Group, whereas a separate Task & Finish Group was convened to compile a preliminary list of controversial terms together with proposed definitions.

title: Deconstruction of Alkali Lignin and Lignocellulosic Substrates by Aspergillus ochraceus DY1 Isolated from Rotten Wood
creator: Namdol Nilza, Ram Prasad, Ajit Varma, Menaka Devi Salam, Baojun Xu
description: The present study reports the ability of a fungal isolate Aspergillus ochraceus DY1, obtained from rotten wood, to degrade alkali lignin (AL) and lignocelluloses in an efficient manner. The efficiency of degradation was monitored by measuring the percentage of decolorization and utilizing GC-MS for identifying degradation products at different time intervals (10, 20, 30, and 40 days).

title: 健康医疗大数据应用的法治风险与规制路径
creator: 金铭 杨, 艳 方, 亚岚 匡, 伟 张, 业勋 胡
description: 随着健康医疗大数据被提升为“国家重要基础性战略资源”，其在公共健康治理、个体权利保障与资源配置优化中的法治意义日益凸显。世界卫生组织（World Health Organization, WHO）《全球数字健康战略（2020–2027年）》提出，数字健康发展应遵循伦理、安全、公平与可持续原则，将数据治理作为实现全民健康权的重要支撑；我国出台《人工智能科技伦理审查与服务办法（试行）》，将生命健康、公共秩序及算法决策等高风险领域纳入全流程伦理审查，初步构建“法治+伦理”的双重规制框架。然而，技术逻辑与法治价值之间仍存在结构性张力，健康医疗大数据应用中逐渐显现出匿名化失灵、算法歧视、数据利益失衡及伦理失范等多重风险。基于此，本文从场景化视角出发，系统识别核心法治风险，并提出分类分级保护、动态匿名化、算法审计及公共利益返还等规制路径，以期在释放数据价值的同时维护数字时代的生命尊严与公共卫生安全。 《“健康中国2030”规划纲要》明确提出推进健康医疗大数据应用，强调加强健康医疗大数据相关法规和标准体系建设，强化数据安全和患者隐私保护[1]。国务院办公厅《关于促进和规范健康医疗大数据应用发展的指导意见》和国家卫生健康委《国家健康医疗大数据标准、安全和服务管理办法（试行）》将健康医疗大数据定位为“国家重要基础性战略资源”[2]。WHO《全球数字健康战略（2020–2027年）》强调，数字健康发展应以伦理、安全、公平和可持续为基本原则[3]。我国《人工智能科技伦理审查与服务办法（试行）》则进一步将生命健康、公共秩序、算法决策等高风险领域纳入伦理审查框架[4]。国务院发布《促进大数据发展行动纲要》，医疗健康服务大数据属于公共服务大数据体系的重要组成部分，涉及公共卫生、医疗服务、医疗保障、药品供应、计划生育和综合管理业务等医疗健康多个领域[5]。 为规范人工智能科技活动伦理治理、防范技术滥用风险，我国正式施行《人工智能科技伦理审查与服务办法（试行）》，明确将对人类生命健康具有较强影响的人机融合系统、具有社会意识引导能力的算法模型、面向高风险场景的高度自主自动化决策系统等纳入伦理审查与专家复核范围，要求遵循增进人类福祉、尊重生命权利、坚持公平公正、合理控制风险、保护隐私安全、确保可控可信等伦理原则，实行全流程伦理审查、跟踪监管与应急审查机制[4]。健康医疗大数据兼具技术共性与法治特殊性，其应用正重塑“风险社会”的法治图景：一是传统知情同意原则在海量数据二次利用中面临功能性失灵，隐私保护防线趋于松动[6-8]；二是技术的黑箱化特征使算法决策可能隐匿歧视与偏见，挑战社会公平正义底线[9-10]；三是当健康数据被视为国家战略资源时，其跨国流动与商业化利用已超出私法范畴，牵动数据主权与国家安全[11-14]。这三重风险相互交织，亟待法治予以系统性回应。 健康医疗大数据应用的法治价值 赋能公共健康治理的价值 健康医疗大数据是公共卫生监测—预警—处置的核心支撑，推动公共卫生推动治理模式由“事后应对”向“事前预测”转型[6]。在宏观层面，通过对人口健康指标、病原特征及环境因素的动态整合分析，政府能够实现风险区域精准识别与医疗资源科学调配。作为具有显著公共属性的数据资源，其在本质上构成国家履行健康权保障义务的重要工具[11, 15]。根据《中华人民共和国宪法》及相关法律的精神，国家负有保障公民健康权的国家保护义务，大数据为传染病监测、风险区域划定、医疗资源调度提供精准依据[7]。WHO在《全球数字健康战略（2020–2027）》中指出，数据驱动的公共卫生治理能够显著提升应急响应效率，是国家履行健康权保障义务的重要技术路径[3]。依托全人群健康监测、病原特征与环境关联分析，政府可精准划定风险区域、优化资源配置，以最小权利克减实现公共利益最大化，构建数字时代公共卫生安全屏障。 美国国家科学院（National Research Council）在Science, Medicine, and Animals中强调，医学研究必须兼顾科研创新与伦理底线，保障受试者及实验对象权益[16]。我国《人工智能科技伦理审查与服务办法（试行）》的实施，则标志着生命伦理审查框架正逐步向人工智能、医疗大数据等新兴技术领域延伸。如相关研究所指出的，科技伦理审查在跨领域适用时面临功能定位模糊与审查形式化风险，亟需结合健康医疗大数据的具体应用场景进行适配性重塑，以确保伦理审查在数智化转型中持续守护生命权与健康权的底线[15]。《人工智能科技伦理审查制度的体系化建构》中所指出，科技伦理审查的核心在于明确制度功能定位、实现跨领域治理协同，避免审查形式化与虚置化问题[11]。源自生命医学领域、以生命伦理为底色的科技伦理审查框架，逐步拓展至人工智能、医疗大数据、智能诊疗系统等新兴技术领域时，亟需对科技伦理审查的功能定位、审查标准与实施机制进行医学场景适配性重塑，推动伦理审查在生命科学、临床医学、人工智能医疗应用等领域形成理念共通、规则衔接、程序协同的一体化治理逻辑，从而在医疗数智化转型中持续坚守对生命权、健康权与人格尊严的底线保障。 促进个体生命权保障与临床科研创新 生命权作为公民最基本的人格权利，其保障程度高度依赖医学科技与数据治理能力的持续提升。健康医疗大数据打破传统医学研究中的 “信息孤岛”，为真实世界研究与精准医疗提供支撑[8, 17]。有研究表明，医疗大数据与人工智能技术有助于缩短新药研发周期并降低研发成本[10]。大数据推动法权保障从“群体概括”走向“精准个体”，同时为医疗损害责任认定提供科学证据，实现程序正义与实质救济统一。WHO于2021年发布的Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health指出，科研数据利用必须以保护隐私与尊重人格为前提，构建数据主体、机构与研究者之间的权利平衡机制[18]。这一价值转换在为科研机构和医疗企业利用数据进行新药研发、罕见病攻关以及精准医疗推演提供了坚实的正当性基础，本质上是在数字空间内通过知识生产的加速来延长人类生命的长度与质量。 同时，大数据还重塑了医疗损害责任认定的证据结构。在复杂医疗纠纷中，基于海量案例的算法分析可提供更具客观性的诊疗参照，促进程序正义与实质正义的统一。在权利结构层面，健康医疗数据的利用亦推动形成“数据利益共享”机制。在去标识化与合规利用前提下，数据得以进入科研体系，实现个人信息自决权与科学研究自由之间的动态平衡，使个体从被动的数据提供者转变为医学进步的参与者。 实现医疗资源分配公平 健康医疗大数据的深度应用，为法治视域下的分配正义提供了一种精准的量化路径，其核心价值在于通过消除信息不对称来矫正医疗资源的结构性失衡[19-20]。在传统的医疗法律关系中，由于缺乏对疾病分布、就医流向及资源负载的实时掌控，医疗资源的配置往往带有一定的盲目性，城乡、区域及阶层间出现了“健康鸿沟”[10]。而大数据的价值在于，通过对全国范围内患病率、就诊半径、药品消耗及医保支付数据的动态分析，提升信息透明度与可计算性，有效矫正医疗资源配置中的结构性失衡。WHO在2022年公平与健康报告指出，数据赋能可显著提升基层医疗服务可及性，推动优质资源下沉[19]。在医保基金监管中，大数据可智能识别骗保、过度诊疗等行为，保障医保基金安全；在分级诊疗与远程医疗中，算法模型将三甲医院诊疗经验向基层延伸，保障公民平等享有优质医疗服务，实现“健康正义”[12, 20-21]。 这种社会正义价值在医保基金监管与分级诊疗制度中表现得尤为突出。在大数据技术的支撑下，国家能够建立起严密的智能审核体系，有效遏制骗保、套保及过度医疗等侵害公共福利资产的行为。这种监管效能的提升，本质上是捍卫了社会保障权的“公平契约”，确保了医保这一公共池塘资源的合规分配。同时，大数据通过赋能远程医疗与基层诊断辅助系统，打破了实体医疗机构的物理边界，原本沉淀在大型三甲医院的优质诊疗经验通过算法模型向基层输送，这在法律层面回应了公民对于平等享有高质量医疗服务权的需求。因此，健康医疗大数据的社会正义价值不仅在于效率的提高，更在于其通过数据赋能，为构建普惠、均衡且具备包容性的数字法治秩序提供了底层逻辑，确保了“健康中国”的建设成果能够跨越数字鸿沟，公平地惠及每一个社会成员[20]。 健康医疗大数据应用的核心风险 临床隐私泄露风险：匿名化失灵与重识别 在健康医疗大数据治理体系中，“匿名化”长期被视为平衡数据流动效率与隐私保护的重要技术路径。在数智化环境下，健康医疗数据的高维、稀疏及强关联特征，使得传统匿名化机制面临“重识别”风险[8, 13, 22]。根据《中华人民共和国个人信息保护法》（以下简称《个人信息保护法》）的规定，经过匿名化处理后的信息因无法识别特定自然人且不能复原，不再被视为个人信息，从而豁免了收集与使用的知情同意义务。然而，在数智化环境的实际应用中，健康医疗大数据的“重识别风险”正使得这一法律隔离墙面临体系性崩塌。健康医疗数据具有高维、稀疏且高度关联的特征，这导致传统法律定义的不可复原在技术层面变得极度脆弱。 首先，“匿名化”定义的法律效力在重识别技术面前陷入崩塌。依据《个人信息保护法》第73条，匿名化需达到“无法识别且不能复原”的绝对标准，但在高维、稀疏的医疗数据面前，攻击者通过辅助信息进行多维碰撞，使得“不可复原性”在技术层面极度脆弱。一旦发生重识别，数据将重新落入敏感个人信息范畴，从而触发更严格的合规义务，形成所谓“规则倒灌”效应。其次，在科学研究与公共卫生场景下，虽存在《个人信息保护法》第13条规定的“法定豁免”事由，但风险在于“目的限制原则”的虚化：一旦采集端以公卫或科研之名获取数据，而在流转端缺乏严格的完整性约束，个体的生物性状与疾病史便可能脱离原始场景，陷入重识威胁。这种从“身份识别”到“特质关联”的风险演变，使得个体的知情自决权在复杂的长链条流转中被实质性剥离，动摇了医疗大数据利用的正当性基础。 这种“匿名化失灵”不仅威胁到个体的人格尊严与生命安全（如因病史泄露导致的就业或保险歧视），更动摇了整个医疗大数据应用的正当性基础。如果法律继续固守单一的、静态的匿名化认定标准，而不转向基于动态风险评估的治理模式，那么所谓的“数据要素市场化”将不可避免地建立在对公民基本权利的超限克减之上。因此，如何在算法重识技术日新月异的背景下，重构法律意义上的“识别性”定义，并从技术治理转向法律责任的归位，已成为健康医疗大数据法治风险治理的首要命题。 根据《个人信息保护法》第73条，匿名化与去标识化具有严格法规差异：匿名化，指无法识别且不可复原，不属于个人信息；去标识化，是指不借助额外信息无法识别，仍属个人信息，受全流程监管。SWEENEY[22]经典研究发现，仅通过出生日期、性别及邮政编码三项信息，即可识别美国87%以上人口身份。研究表明即便医疗数据经过去标识化处理，攻击者仍可能通过辅助信息进行多维碰撞，从而重新识别特定个体。WHO《Data Privacy Framework for Health Data》特别指出，健康医疗数据的重识别风险远高于普通个人信息，必须实施更高等级的数据保护措施[13]。在科研、公卫、商业场景中，合法性基础应严格区分：公卫与科研可适用法定豁免，但严禁目的漂移与跨场景滥用；商业利用必须坚持单独同意，禁止以公益名义攫取私益[6-8]。 数智技术风险：算法黑箱与数字歧视 当健康医疗大数据从单纯的存储资源转化为驱动临床决策与公共管理的算法模型时，法治风险也随之从数据安全层面跃升至分配正义层面[9-10]。OBERMEYER等[9]研究发现，美国医疗资源分配算法存在明显种族偏差，同等健康状况下，黑人患者获得高风险评估的概率显著低于白人患者。患者算法偏见并非单纯的技术偶发事件，而是社会既有偏见在数字空间的镜像投射与放大，在医疗场景下，这种偏见往往转化为系统性的“数字歧视”，严重侵蚀了法治社会关于平等权与公正原则的底线。 算法偏见的危机首先源于样本偏差导致的结果不公。如果训练医疗人工智能（AI）的数据集主要源于特定经济水平或族裔群体，那么算法在面对边缘群体或少数族群时，其预测精度将显著下降。例如，若心脏病预测模型主要基于男性数据，则可能在女性患者身上表现出极高的误诊率。这种基于身份特征的差异化对待，在法律上构成了间接歧视。更为严峻的是，这种歧视往往隐匿在“黑箱”式的算法逻辑中，具有极强的隐蔽性与不可追责性。当医院利用算法分配重症监护室（ICU）病床，或保险公司利用大数据预测个体的长期患病风险并据此实行差异化定价时，个体往往无法感知自己正处于不公正的待遇中。算法“黑箱”特征使患者难以理解医疗决策逻辑，进一步压缩患者知情权、申诉权及公平医疗权[10, 18]。WHO在Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health中指出，医疗AI治理必须强调可解释性、公平性与可追责性，以避免形成新的数字等级制度[18]。 这种数字歧视直接挑战了现代法治的责任归属体系。传统法律体系建立在“过错归责”基础之上，要求受害方证明加害方的恶意或疏忽，然而，在算法驱动的医疗决策中，歧视往往是自动生成的，甚至连算法开发人员也难以解释决策的因果链条。这种决策的不可解释性，导致患者的知情权与申诉权在技术壁垒面前全面溃缩。如果法律不能确立算法的可解释性标准，那么健康医疗大数据的广泛应用极易形成一种新型的数字等级制度。 数据流转风险：生物安全与公共利益流失 从宏观维度审视，健康医疗大数据因其“国家重要基础性战略资源”的定性，其风险边界已大幅超越了个体私权的范畴，上升至国家主权安全与公共利益分配的高度[8]。在数据要素的频繁流转与跨境应用中，如何防范核心战略资源的流失与异化，构成了法治风险解析中不可忽视的命题。 健康医疗大数据不仅关涉个体隐私，更涉及国家数字主权、生物安全与公共利益分配问题[11-14]。WHO在全球健康安全相关报告中强调，健康数据跨境流动必须经过严格安全评估，防范种群遗传信息泄露与滥用[13]。健康数据不仅包含个体的临床记录，更涵盖了大规模的种群遗传信息、基因序列及生物族群的分布特征。在数据要素市场化背景下，若缺乏收益返还机制，则容易导致“公共资源私有化”，形成公众承担隐私风险、资本独占数据收益的失衡风险[14,

title: Thermal Oscillations of Nanobubbles
creator: Duncan Dockar, Livio Gibelli, Matthew K Borg
description: Nanobubble cavitation is advancing technologies in enhanced wastewater treatment, cancer therapy and diagnosis, and microfluidic cleaning. Current macroscale models predict that nanobubble oscillations should be isothermal, yet recent studies suggest that they are adiabatic with an associated increase in natural frequency, which becomes challenging when characterizing nanobubble sizes using ultrasound in experiments.

title: Confirmatory factor analysis of competing PANSS negative symptom models: data from OPTiMiSE first-episode schizophrenia study
creator: Arsime Demjaha, Daniel Stahl, Celso Arango, Birte Glenthøj, Roberto Rodriguez-Jimenez, Covadonga Martinez Díaz-Caneja, Lone Baandrup, Bjørn Ebdrup, Maria Paz Garcia-Portlla, Maria Diaz-Marsa, Inge Winter-van Rossum, Rene Kahn, Paola Dazzan, Philip McGuire
description: BackgroundThe negative symptoms of psychosis are heterogeneous, which complicates efforts to understand their pathophysiology and develop effective treatments. Factor analytic studies of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) have reported two factorial negative symptom models, expressive deficit and social amotivation, albeit with different compositions.

title: Minimally Invasive Fixation of a Distal Fibula Fracture With an Intramedullary Nail
creator: Jothi Murali-Larson, Jocelyn R Wittstein, Jennifer Beck, Claudia Arias, Camille Coates-Clark
description: Background:Advantages of using an intramedullary (IM) nail over a lateral plate for fixation of distal fibula fractures include the ability to allow for earlier weightbearing and return to sport, smaller incisions, and decreased hardware prominence. When comparing a fibular nail with an IM screw, the nail allows for syndesmosis fixation through the device and imparts rotational stability.

title: Dynamic-Cross-Linked, Regulated, and Controllable Mineralization Degree and Morphology of Collagen Biomineralization
creator: Ziyao Geng, Fan Xu, Ying Liu, Aike Qiao, Tianming Du
description: The cross-linking process of collagen is one of the more important ways to improve the mineralization ability of collagen. However, the regulatory effect of dynamic cross-linking on biomineralization in vitro remains unclear. Dynamic-cross-linked mineralized collagen under different cross-linking processes, according to the process of cross-linking and mineralization of natural bone, was prepared in this study.

title: 3D Liquid Crystal Framework Enclosing Dual Compartments
creator: Yang‐yang Zhao, Huan‐jun Lu, Helgard Ebert, Xiang‐bing Zeng, Chunlan Ma, Feng Liu, Carsten Tschierske, Goran Ungar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We report a new 3D‐ordered liquid‐crystal (LC) phase where alkyl and fluoroalkyl side‐chains are confined within separate stretched octahedral cages of a tetragonal framework with struts of aromatic rods held together by their hydrogen‐bonded ends acting as flexible hinges. This is the first example of a multicolor micellar LC heralding the development of soft and dynamic dual‐compartment frameworks, also capable of a martensitic‐type phase transition.

title: Improvement of restless leg syndrome in maintenance hemodialysis patients with limb ischemic preconditioning: a single-center randomized controlled clinical trial
creator: Juntian Xu, Yuan Qi, Yushang Tang, Wanfen Zhang, Qiaoyang Zhang, Linfang Xu, Zhongqin Ding, Tongqiang Liu
description: ObjectiveThis study evaluated the efficacy and safety of limb ischemic preconditioning (LIPC) in treating restless leg syndrome (RLS) in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients.MethodsA total number of 45 patients participated in the study. They were randomly divided into LIPC group and control group.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Halitosis Among University Students in Guangxi, Southern China: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Haishan Zhang, Tingting Zhang, Xingguo Fu, Honglin Qin, Xiaochun Chen, Xiaojuan Zeng
description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the prevalence of halitosis and explore associated factors among university students in Guangxi, Southern China.Materials and MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among university students aged 18–25 from 10 universities in Guangxi using multi-stage stratified random sampling. Face-to-face, paper-based questionnaires were administered to collect participants’ general information and data on self-reported halitosis.

title: Impact of Intermittent Deposition on Spontaneous Orientation Polarization of Organic Amorphous Films Revealed by Rotary Kelvin Probe
creator: Masahiro Ohara, Hokuto Hamada, Noritaka Matsuura, Yuya Tanaka, Hisao Ishii
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The control of the molecular orientation and resultant polarization is essential for improving the performance of organic optoelectronic devices. Conventionally, the substrate temperature and deposition rate are tuned to control the molecular orientation of vapor-deposited films. In this study, we proposed a novel method, referred to as “intermittent deposition”, in which the polarization direction and magnitude are controlled by introducing intervals during physical vapor deposition.

title: Addressing bioenergetic deficits and restoring mitochondrial health in transplanted islets using mesenchymal stem cells
creator: Rosita Primavera, Abantika Ganguly, Reza Yarani, Lili Bettencourt, Shobha Regmi, Shashank Chetty, Jing Wang, Michele Guindani, Ramasamy Paulmurugan, Avnesh S Thakor
description: During the process of islet transplantation, islets undergo isolation and are then introduced into a new microenvironment where they need to adapt and revascularize. This transition imposes substantial stress on islets, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, adversely affecting islet function and vitality.

title: Discovery and Characterization of an Atypical Crustin Antimicrobial Peptide from Pollicipes pollicipes
creator: Wei Zhang, Liumi Wei, Pengyu Chen, Biao Ning, Junjian Wang, Peng He, Chenjing Shang, Dahui Yu, Fernando Albericio, Tatiana V Ovchinnikova
description: Crustins are a family of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that play a pivotal role in the innate immune system of crustaceans. The discovery of novel AMPs from natural sources is crucial for expanding our current database of these peptides. Here, we identified and characterized a novel member of the crustin family, named PpCrus-SWD1, derived from Pollicipes pollicipes.

title: A plain language review of the ATTRibute-CM study: efficacy and safety of acoramidis in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy
creator: Julian D. Gillmore, Daniel P. Judge, Francesco Cappelli, Marianna Fontana, Pablo Garcia-Pavia, Simon Gibbs, Martha Grogan, Mazen Hanna, James Hoffman, Ahmad Masri, Mathew S. Maurer, Jose Nativi-Nicolau, Laura Obici, Steen Hvitfeldt Poulsen, Frank Rockhold, Keyur B. Shah, Prem Soman, Jyotsna Garg, Ka
description: Plain Language Summary What is this plain language review about? This plain language review describes the results of a study called ATTRibute-CM. This study looked at how well a drug called acoramidis worked to treat people with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM).

title: Plasma Gelation as an Overlooked Determinant of Transfection Efficiency in Protein Corona‐Coated Lipid Nanoparticles: Implications for In Vitro–In Vivo Translation
creator: Serena Renzi, Luca Digiacomo, Francesca Giulimondi, Daniela Pozzi, Junbiao Wang, Augusto Amici, Cristina Marchini, Chiara Cassone, Alessandra Zingoni, Fabrizio Marra, Luca Buccini, Francesco Mura, Valentina De Lorenzi, Francesco Cardarelli, Giulio Caracciolo
description: A common observation in drug delivery studies is that preincubation of nanoparticles (NPs) with high concentrations of human plasma (HP) markedly reduces in vitro transfection efficiency (TE). This effect is commonly attributed to the formation of a protein corona (PC), which is assumed to impair cellular uptake or intracellular trafficking of gene delivery systems such as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs).

title: Breastfeeding duration and associations with prevention of accelerated growth among infants from low-income, racially and ethnically diverse backgrounds
creator: Jigna M Dharod, Christina M Frazier, Jeffery Labban, Maureen M Black
description: Objective:To describe breastfeeding rates from early to late infancy and to examine associations between breastfeeding duration and infant growth, including rapid weight gain (RWG, > 0·67 SD increase in weight-for-age Z-score), among infants from low-income, racially and ethnically diverse backgrounds.Design:A short, prospective cohort study was conducted assessing breastfeeding status at infant ages 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12 months.

title: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound regulates the osteogenic–adipogenic differentiation balance of rat adipose-derived stem cells via the PI3K/AKT-SREBF1 signaling axis
creator: Wenzhong Hu, Zhihao Zhao, Qiuling Zhang, Pei Gong, Xinyu Wang, Cong Han, Xinzhe Gao, Jie Long
description: Rat adipose-derived stem cells (rADSCs) are widely used in bone tissue engineering (BTE). Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) can modulate stem cell fate; however, its precise regulatory effects on ADSC lineage commitment remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate how LIPUS regulates the osteogenic–adipogenic differentiation balance of rADSCs.

title: Biomimetic Proteoglycans for Intervertebral Disc (IVD) Regeneration
creator: Neha Chopra, James Melrose, Zi Gu, Ashish D. Diwan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Intervertebral disc degeneration, which leads to low back pain, is the most prevalent musculoskeletal condition worldwide, significantly impairing quality of life and imposing substantial socioeconomic burdens on affected individuals. A major impediment to the development of any prospective cell-driven recovery of functional properties in degenerate IVDs is the diminishing IVD cell numbers and viability with ageing which cannot sustain such a recovery process.

title: Maladaptive exercise: the hidden role of physical activity and sport professionals in the early detection of eating disorders
creator: Valerio Zaccaria, Fabiola Panvino, Roberto Paparella, Maura Ilardi, Dolores Forgione, Ignazio Ardizzone, Francesco Pisani
description: Eating disorders (EDs) are a significant public health concern, particularly among adolescents and young adults. While physical activity (PA) is generally health-promoting, maladaptive exercise, characterized by compulsive and excessive activity linked to weight control, is often a core feature of ED pathology.

title: Cognitive disengagement syndrome and peer relationships of youth with critical congenital heart defects
creator: Olivia G Ritchey, Eva L Darow, Amber T Riggs, Andrea Goard, Jamie L Jackson, May Ling Mah, H Gerry Taylor, Kathryn Kirkpatrick, Kathryn Vannatta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Worldwide, approximately 1 in 100 children are born with a congenital heart defect, with 25% of those being classified as critical and posing risks for neurocognitive deficits due to cyanosis. Cognitive Disengagement Syndrome (CDS) has yet to be examined in children with critical congenital heart defects (cCHD) despite calls for research in pediatric populations with acquired brain injury and associated deficits.

title: Evaluating completeness, coherence, and consistency of genome-scale function annotations
creator: Rund Tawfiq, Maxat Kulmanov, Robert Hoehndorf
description: Protein function annotation traditionally follows a reductionist approach, assigning functions to individual proteins acting in isolation. This treats each annotation as an independent fact, disconnected from the broader biological system. However, proteins operate within integrated networks where their functions depend on genomic context and interacting partners. This needs to be reflected in function annotation and evaluation frameworks.

title: Endovascular Repair of a Failed Nellix Endograft Proximal Sealing Zone Using the Altura Stent-Graft: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Dimitrios A. Chatzelas, Apostolos G. Pitoulias, Georgios V. Tsamourlidis, Theodosia N. Zampaka, Anastasios G. Potouridis, Maria D. Tachtsi, Georgios A. Pitoulias
description: Endovascular aortic aneurysm sealing (EVAS) with the Nellix endograft was initially considered a groundbreaking and acceptable alternative to conventional endovascular aortic aneurysm repair, with encouraging initial results. However, long-term follow-up has revealed a high incidence of endograft-related complications, such as caudal migration and type Ia endoleaks, indicating the need for reintervention.

title: Animals as Architects: Building the Future of Technology-Supported Rehabilitation with Biomimetic Principles
creator: Bruno Bonnechère
description: Rehabilitation science has evolved significantly with the integration of technology-supported interventions, offering objective assessments, personalized programs, and real-time feedback for patients. Despite these advances, challenges remain in fully addressing the complexities of human recovery through the rehabilitation process. Over the last few years, there has been a growing interest in the application of biomimetics to inspire technological innovation.

title: Drivers of the paradigm shift in norovirus diagnostics: technological innovation, contextual demands, and collaborative synergy
creator: Zhou Peng, Xinlan Zhang, Xiyan Deng, Defu Hou, Rushi Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper systematically reviews paradigm shifts in diagnostic technologies for norovirus. Given the substantial burden of acute gastroenteritis caused by this virus and the current lack of licensed antiviral therapies, early and accurate diagnosis is of paramount importance. Diagnostic technologies have evolved from electron microscopy and immunological assays to molecular detection methods, with reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) currently recognized as the gold standard for molecular diagnostics.

title: Mechanistic insights into how water-network disorder determines the vitrification concentration in cryopreservation solutions
creator: Euihyun Lee, Nora Gaby-Biegel, Rebecca D Sandlin, Carlos R Baiz
description: SUMMARYCryopreservation enables long-term storage of biological materials using cryoprotective agents (CPAs) to suppress ice crystal formation and prevent cell damage. However, despite considerable efforts, a molecular-level understanding of how CPAs prevent ice-crystal formation has not yet been established, particularly one that generalizes across different CPAs.

title: Sex-related upregulation of bone morphogenetic protein signaling inhibits adult neurogenesis in APPNL−G−F alzheimer’s disease model mice
creator: Xingyu Su, Rina Takayanagi, Hiroki Maeda, Takaomi C. Saido, Toshio Ohshima
description: BackgroundBone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) have been reported in many studies to be related to adult neurogenesis. Neurogenic impairment is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), while the involvement of BMPs remains unclear.MethodsAD models were established using APPNL−G−F transgenic mice and C57BL/6 mice subjected to intracerebral injection of Aβ(25–35) peptide.

title: The association between mental healthcare professionals’ personal characteristics and their clinical lifestyle practices: a national cross-sectional study in The Netherlands
creator: Lisanne E.M. Koomen, Jeroen Deenik, Wiepke Cahn
description: BackgroundLifestyle interventions are important to improve the mental and physical health outcomes of people with mental illness. However, referring patients to lifestyle interventions is still not a common practice for mental healthcare professionals (MHCPs) and their own lifestyle habits may impact this.

title: High Fracture Risk of Femoral Bone Metastasis Treated with Palliative Radiotherapy in Recent Years
creator: Kenji Makita, Hidehiro Hojo, Hidekazu Oyoshi, Takeshi Fujisawa, Masaki Nakamura, Gyo Uchida, Yume Koike, Yuzheng Zhou, Kento Tomizawa, Keiko Fukushi, Sadamoto Zenda
description: Bone-modifying agents (BMAs) have been widely used to reduce skeletal-related events, including pathological fractures. Herein, we aimed to clarify the incidence of pathological fractures caused by high-risk femoral bone metastases after palliative radiotherapy (RT) in the BMA era and evaluate the necessity of prophylactic surgical stabilization.

title: Implementation components and delivery structures of adolescent peer navigation as a workforce model: a scoping review
creator: Ashley Chory, Ava Boal, Annabel Azziz, Carrie Levinson, Lonnie Embleton, Mary Ott, Rachel Vreeman, Edith Apondi
description: BackgroundAdolescents face persistent barriers to accessing health services, particularly among vulnerable populations such as those living with HIV, adolescent mothers, and youth experiencing mental health or substance use challenges. Peer navigation has emerged as a promising strategy to address these gaps by leveraging shared lived experience to support engagement across health and social systems.

title: 13C NMR as a foundation for machine learning models of polysaccharides
creator: Stephanann M Costello, Zeina C Sleiman, John N Glushka, Breeanna R Urbanowicz, Arthur S Edison
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Polysaccharide structural assignment via nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy remains an analytical challenge due to spectral overlap because of limited chemical shift dispersion. This challenge is exacerbated by the wide-spread use of proton (1H) detection. Progress has also been hindered by the dispersed nature of carbohydrate databases and the restricted applicability of most prediction tools, which provide limited atom-specific residue discrimination in larger polymers.

title: CD248, targeted by veratramine and neobavaisoflavone, mediates pathological changes of renal tubular epithelial cells induced by high glucose
creator: Mei Lin, Nan Hu, Zhen Wang, Ping Li, Dan Song, Xinzhou Zhang
description: BackgroundEpithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of tubular epithelial cells are one of the major pathological changes of diabetic nephropathy (DN). Cluster of differentiation 248 (CD248) has been reported to be associated with fibrosis after kidney injury. The aim of this study was to investigate the mechanism of CD248 in DN and its targeted compounds.

title: Report of high data rate macromolecular crystallography (HDRMX) meeting, 23 July 2025
creator: Christine Beavers, Herbert J. Bernstein, Aaron S. Brewster, Max Burian, Nicholas Devenish, Jiaxin Dawn Duan, Daniel Eriksson, Diego Gämperle, Yang Ha, David R. Hall, James Holton, Peter Keller, Loes Kroon-Batenburg, David W. Mittan-Moreau, Yasukazu Nakaye, Daniel W. Paley, Ezra Peisach, Nicholas K.
description: This paper is a report of the High Data Rate Macromolecular Crystallography workshop held on 23 July 2025 as part of the 2025 meeting of the American Crystallographic Association in Lombard, IL, USA, 18–23 July 2025. This report summarizes the discussions, questions, action items, and recommendations that arose from the meeting and includes links to the presentations.

title: Diverging transposon activity among polar bear sub-populations inhabiting different climate zones
creator: Alice M Godden, Benjamin T Rix, Simone Immler
description: A new subpopulation of polar bears (Ursus maritimus) was recently discovered in the South-East of Greenland. This isolated colony inhabits a warmer climate zone, akin to the predicted future environments of polar bears with vastly reduced sea ice habitats, rendering this population of bears particularly important.

title: Multicenter, prospective cohort study: immediate postoperative gains in active range of motion following robotic-assisted total knee replacement compared to a propensity-matched control using manual instrumentation
creator: Camdon Fary, Jason Cholewa, Anna N Ren, Scott Abshagen, Mike B Anderson, Krishna Tripuraneni
description: BackgroundRange of motion (ROM) following total knee replacement (TKR) has been associated with patient satisfaction and knee function, and is also an early indicator of a successful procedure. Robotic-assisted TKR (raTKR) is considered to reproduce more precise resections, and, as a result, may be associated with improved early patient satisfaction compared to manual TKR (mTKR).

title: Physicians’ perspectives on artificial intelligence in electrocardiography in clinical practice: a qualitative study
creator: Gabriel Allgårdh, Gert Helgesson, Ulrik Kihlbom
description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may support ECG interpretation, prioritization, and workflow efficiency. ECGs are widely used, inexpensive, and often obtained with a low clinical threshold, meaning that AI-ECG may affect large numbers of patients and reshape an established clinical workflow. This study explored physician’s perspectives on integrating AI-ECG into clinical practice.

title: A Review of White Spot Lesions: Development and Treatment with Resin Infiltration
creator: Alexandra Maria Prada, Georgiana Ioana Potra Cicalău, Gabriela Ciavoi
description: White spot lesions (WSLs) are demineralized lesions of the enamel that form in the presence of bacterial plaque, affecting the aesthetics by modifying the refractive index of the enamel, giving the characteristic “chalky” aspect. They have various causes, including fixed orthodontic treatments, improper hygiene, fluorosis and genetic factors.

title: Global burden of ovarian cancer attributable to high BMI, 1990–2021: spatiotemporal trends, risk factors, frontier analysis, and projections to 2036 based on GBD 2021 study
creator: Jiujie He, Wanting Zhou, Yujun He, Yingjie Nie, Hua Qiu, Wei Mai
description: BackgroundDespite the well-established link between elevated body mass index (BMI) and ovarian cancer, comprehensive global assessments of the attributable burden remain scarce. Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 database, we quantified deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) from ovarian cancer due to high BMI between 1990 and 2021 and delineated spatiotemporal trends to inform targeted prevention.

title: Clinical outcomes of capitellar fractures with posterior comminution treated with Herbert screws combined with metacarpal locking plates
creator: Xiang Gao, Hang Li, Deting Xue, Zhijun Pan, Yujie Zhang
description: BackgroundThe treatment of Dubberley type B capitellar fractures, which are frequently complicated, is widely debated. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic factors and clinical outcomes of Dubberley type B capitellar fractures treated with Herbert screws combined with posterior buttress plates.

title: Short‐Term Exposure of Bisphenol A Deteriorates the Quality of Rabbit Milk by Impairing Milk Fat Synthesis
creator: Jia Hao, Shaohui Beng, Zifeng Ma, Hongmei Xu, Ting Yang, Qiman Yang, Yunduan Wang, Wenhui Zheng, Yisha Ma, Shuo Zhang, Liangde Kuang, Wei Fu
description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of short‐term exposure of Bisphenol A (BPA) on the growth and lactation performance, blood parameters, and milk composition of lactating rabbits and explore its potential molecular mechanisms. Eight lactating rabbits with similar body weight were selected and randomly divided into the experimental group (BPA) and the control group (Ctrl).

title: A next-generation sequencing approach for high-resolution S-locus genotyping in apricot
creator: Jorge Lora, Andrea Torres, José I. Hormaza, Javier Rodrigo, Afif Hedhly
description: Most temperate fruit crops exhibit a Gametophytic Self-Incompatibility (GSI) mechanism that prevents incompatible pollen tube growth and promotes outbreeding. In Prunus species, this system is governed by the multiallelic S-locus, which contains the S-haplotype-specific F-box (SFB) and S-RNase genes. Accurate determination of S-haplotypes is important for fruit breeding and orchard design and has traditionally relied on PCR-based analysis.

title: Impulsivity‐Related Traits in Eating Disorders With Self‐Harm or Suicidal Behaviour: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
creator: Maria Gemescu, Cezar Giosan, Ana Maria Olguța Barizi, Carmen‐Andreea Petre, Ana‐Alecsandra Gușoaie, Elena‐Luiza Costache, Ana‐Patricia Darabont, Teodora‐Maria Neagoe, Rareș‐Mihnea Iosifescu
description: BackgroundAlthough impulsivity is commonly associated with eating disorders (EDs) comorbid with self‐harm, no prior reviews have investigated whether ED groups with co‐occurring self‐harm exhibit increased impulsivity‐related traits.ObjectiveThis systematic review and meta‐analysis synthesized the differences between ED groups with vs. without self‐harm/suicidal behaviour, with respect to impulsivity‐related domains.

title: Characterization and inhibition of inflammasome responses in severe and non-severe asthma
creator: Jay C. Horvat, Richard Y. Kim, Natasha Weaver, Christopher Augood, Alexandra C. Brown, Chantal Donovan, Pierrick Dupre, Lakshitha Gunawardhana, Jemma R. Mayall, Nicole G. Hansbro, Avril A. B. Robertson, Luke A. J. O’Neill, Matthew A. Cooper, Elizabeth G. Holliday, Philip M. Hansbro, Peter G. Gibson
description: BackgroundIncreased airway NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated IL-1β responses may underpin severe neutrophilic asthma. However, whether increased inflammasome activation is unique to severe asthma, is a common feature of immune cells in all inflammatory types of severe asthma, and whether inflammasome activation can be therapeutically targeted in patients, remains unknown.

title: Optimization of Ultrasound Extraction of Total Anthocyanin From Berberis kaschgarica Rupr. by Response Surface Methodology and Its Antihypertensive Effect
creator: Nawaz Khan, Maierdan Yusufu, Zeynab Ahmadova, Nulibiya Maihemuti, Sendaer Hailati, Ziruo Talihat, Nuerbiye Nueraihemaiti, Dilihuma Dilimulati, Alhar Baishan, Li Duan, Wenting Zhou
description: Berberis kaschgarica Rupr. is a berry fruit shrub found in the north‐western region of China, locally its fruit is consumed as a tea ingredient a part of the daily diet, for treatment of different diseases like eczema, and for cardiovascular care as a traditional remedy.

title: Enhancing PARP inhibitor efficacy in ovarian cancer: targeting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway
creator: Yixuan Wang, Qing Xia, Xinjia Wang, Yiwei Lu, Shizhuo Wang, Yisheng Jiao
description: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most lethal gynecologic malignancies, often marked by late-stage diagnosis and resistance to conventional therapies. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors have significantly advanced treatment, particularly in tumors with homologous recombination deficiencies, such as BRCA1/2 mutations.

title: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery
creator: Zihao Wen, Mengxin Xu, Zijun Yan, Ziren Kong, Yupeng Wang, Pei Liu, Junyi Chen, Yanzhao Liu, Xi-Yang Cui, Tianyi Cen, Xinwei Li, Yuedan Zheng, Zichen Gu, Da Xu, Qiang Xu, Yaping Luo, Changlun Wang, Zhibo Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Drug conjugates, such as antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) and small molecule–drug conjugates (SMDCs), are often dependent on efficient receptor-mediated endocytosis for payload release1–3—supported by about 10% of targets4–7. For poorly internalizing targets, drug conjugates dissociate and clear rapidly, limiting efficacy. To overcome the limitation in the internalization-to-release (ITR) pattern, we introduce a binding-to-release (BTR) strategy that decouples drug release from endocytosis by positioning an electrophile for direct cleavage by a proximal nucleophilic residue within the binding pocket.

title: Pseudoaneurysm of mitral-aortic intervalvular fibrosa with rupture: a case report
creator: Kosuke Nakata, Shuji Moriyama, Jun Takaki, Masahiro Takeo, Hideki Doi, Toshiyuki Matsumura, Toshihiro Fukui
description: BackgroundMitral-aortic intervalvular fibrosa (MAIVF) is a fibrous region connecting the anterior mitral leaflet (AML) and aortic valve. Pseudoaneurysm of the MAIVF is a rare condition that has been reported as a sequela of infective endocarditis (IE) and surgical trauma. Here, we report a case of a ruptured pseudoaneurysm of the MAIVF, along with some literature reviews.

title: Cannabidiol does not cause DNA double-strand breaks in a human liver-derived cell model
creator: Romano Weiss, Victoria Liedtke, Stefan Rödiger
description: BackgroundCannabidiol (CBD) is a non-psychoactive cannabinoid with potential therapeutic applications, including anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and anticancer effects. However, experts raised concerns about its potential to induce DNA damage and chromosomal aberrations at low concentrations. Notably, these studies used liver cell lines, which may not fully reflect the metabolic processing of CBD, potentially limiting the generalizability of their findings.

title: The Ripple Effect: Aftereffects and Social Consequences of Organ Donation Decisions
creator: Vijay Tadia, Parul Gupta
description: Context:Organ donation represents a profound act of compassion and solidarity, offering hope to those grappling with end stage organ failure. While many families ultimately choose to proceed with organ donation, a significant portion remains hesitant or outrightly refuse. The ripples of the decision to donate organs are felt for a long time after the decision has been undertaken.

title: Dynamics of the oral microbiome during orthodontic treatment and antimicrobial advances for orthodontic appliances
creator: Qin Niu, Si Chen, Rushui Bai, Yuntao Lu, Liying Peng, Bing Han, Tingting Yu
description: SummaryThe oral microbiome plays an important role in human health, and an imbalance of the oral microbiome could lead to oral and systemic diseases. Orthodontic treatment is an effective method to correct malocclusion. However, it is associated with many adverse effects, including white spot lesions, caries, gingivitis, periodontitis, halitosis, and even some systematic diseases.

title: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm
creator: Regev Schweiger, Sangjin Lee, Chenxi Zhou, Tsun-Po Yang, Stacy Li, Rashesh Sanghvi, Matthew Neville, Katie Smith, Kirsty Roberts, Ayrun Nessa, Sam Wadge, Kerrin S. Small, Peter J. Campbell, Kristian Almstrup, Peter H. Sudmant, Raheleh Rahbari, Richard Durbin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Meiotic recombination is a fundamental process that generates genetic diversity by creating new combinations of existing alleles1. Whereas crossovers in humans are well characterized2, the more frequent non-crossovers that lead to gene conversion remain challenging to study. Here we show that single high-fidelity long sequencing reads from sperm can capture both crossovers and non-crossovers, which enables effectively arbitrary sample sizes for analysis from a single male.

title: Regulation of the cell division hydrolase RipC by the FtsEX system in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
creator: Jianwei Li, Xin Xu, Jian Shi, Juan A. Hermoso, Lok-To Sham, Min Luo
description: The FtsEX complex regulates, directly or via a protein mediator depending on bacterial genera, peptidoglycan degradation for cell division. In mycobacteria and Gram-positive bacteria, the FtsEX system directly activates peptidoglycan-hydrolases by a mechanism that remains unclear. Here we report our investigation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis FtsEX as a non-canonical regulator with high basal ATPase activity.

title: Aberrant excitatory neuronal ERBB4 promotes Alzheimer’s disease pathology
creator: Se Young Lee, Eunseok Park, Ha-Eun Lee, Seongbin Kim, Yeji Yeo, Juwon Park, Young-Jin Choi, Kiheon Lee, Ki-Jun Yoon, Sanghoon Park, Eunjoon Kim, Jae-Ick Kim, Won-Suk Chung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neuroinflammation and synapse loss are associated with cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Although microglial hyperphagocytic activity has been implicated in synapse loss1–4, the mechanisms underlying these pathologies remain obscure. Here we demonstrate that, during AD progression in mice, astrocytes and microglia increase phagocytic elimination of excitatory synapses while reducing elimination of inhibitory synapses, suggesting that neuroinflammation alone may be dispensable for early AD synapse loss.

title: HapAsmbl: A reference‐aided pipeline for assembling haplotypes in Nanopore amplicon sequence data of polymorphic populations
creator: Ayodele Oluwaseyi Fakoya, Augustine Chen, Rowan Paul Herridge, Richard Colin Macknight, Lynette Ruth Brownfield
description: PremiseAdvances in long‐read sequencing offer new possibilities to investigate haplotype diversity across multiple genes in plants and other taxa through multi‐locus, long‐read amplicon sequencing (multi‐locus LRAS). Despite this progress, there is a notable absence of dedicated bioinformatics pipelines for assembling diploid haplotypes of heterozygous individuals from such multi‐locus LRAS datasets, which is required for highly polymorphic populations.

title: Lessons learned from responses to COVID-19 pandemic in rural, Indigenous, and isolated populations in the US and India: a qualitative study
creator: Austin Henderson, Tenzin Namdul, Gary Ferguson, Sara London, Richard MacLehose, Dedra Buchwald
description: BackgroundRural, Indigenous, and isolated communities faced unique challenges and opportunities during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. Identifying lessons from these communities, which are rarely studied, is crucial for improving future crisis responses similar populations. This study aims to inform similar communities by centralizing lessons learned and improving preparedness for future health crises.

title: Developing a hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) gynecologic oncology program: a Canadian experience
creator: Joannie Neveu, Elizabeth Tremblay, Frederic Mercier, Sébastien Garneau, Beatrice Cormier
description: Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) is a treatment option for epithelial ovarian cancer following cytoreductive surgery. The intraperitoneal spread of the disease makes the peritoneal cavity an ideal target for drug delivery. HIPEC has shown promising results in improving overall survival in epithelial ovarian cancer patients when performed during interval cytoreductive surgery.

title: Benefits of hip arthroscopy surgery for soccer players: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Wenbo Zhao, Zihan Zhou, Yang Li, Changquan Wang
description: BackgroundThe complex and dynamic biomechanics of soccer significantly increase the susceptibility of the hip joint to injury. While hip arthroscopy is a valuable diagnostic and therapeutic modality that facilitates an expedited return to play for athletes, the specific extent of its clinical benefit for soccer players requires further evaluation.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted.

title: Real-world data on niraparib maintenance treatment in patients with non-gBRCA mutated platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer
creator: Bente Vilming, Jørgen Fallås Dahl, Anne Gry Bentzen, Vibeke Anett Ingebrigtsen, Elisabeth Berge Nilsen, Ingvild Vistad, Anne Dørum, Olesya Solheim, Line Bjørge, Manuela Zucknick, Guro Aune, Kristina Lindemann
description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to provide real-world efficacy and safety data on niraparib maintenance treatment in patients with non-germline (gBRCA)1/2 mutated platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer.MethodsThis retrospective multi-center cohort study included 94 platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer patients without known gBRCA1/2 mutation treated in an individual patient access program in Norway.

title: scTumorDrug: predicting cell-type-specific drug responses for heterogeneous tumors
creator: Qiang Zhang, Qing Zhang, Chunming Guo, Cheng Peng
description: It is important to predict cell-type-specific drug responses within the heterogeneous tumors for precision medicine. The single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technique together with drug responses data provides opportunities for this mission. The previous methods were mainly evaluated in datasets derived from cancer cell lines, lacking direct validations on the real tumors derived from mouse models and clinical human samples.

title: Visual image perception preservation through a compression-encryption framework
creator: Marwa E. Madkour, Salah E. Soliman, Moawad. I. Dessouky, Fathi E. Abd El-Samie, Amir S. Elsafrawey, Mohammed E. Hammad
description: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are increasingly deployed for monitoring both one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) environmental phenomena, generating vast amounts of sensitive data, often in the form of images, which are transmitted daily. Ensuring secure data transmission over untrusted communication channels is a persistent and critical challenge.

title: The paradox of agency in psychotherapy: How people with mental distress experience support from generative AI chatbots and human therapists
creator: Xiaolu Dai, Ling Li Leng, Yiyan Liu, Yu-Te Huang, Daniel Fu Keung Wong
description: BackgroundThe rapid advancement of Large Language Models has sparked heated debate over whether Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots can serve as “digital therapists” capable of providing therapeutic support. While much of this discussion focuses on AI’s lack of agency, understood as the absence of mental states, consciousness, autonomy, and intentionality, empirical research on users’ real-world experiences remains limited.

title: ZIKV NS3 disrupts Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense and drives vascular smooth muscle cell damage and vascular dysfunction
creator: Ren-Hua Yang, Wen-Cong Gao, Li Zhang, Tian-Zhang Song, Rong-Hua Luo, Ting Zhang, Liu-Meng Yang, Yong-Tang Zheng, Chang-Bo Zheng, Peng Chen
description: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection has been linked to vascular complications, yet the basis of vascular injury after apparent clearance of circulating virus remains poorly understood. This study examined the temporal progression of ZIKV-associated vascular damage and defined the contribution of non-structural protein 3 (NS3) to oxidative stress-mediated vascular dysfunction.

title: RTEL1 mutation modifies dyskeratosis congenita caused by a telomerase RNA template mutation
creator: Nathaniel Deimler, Alex Orioli, Laura Holthöfer, Matthias Linke, Nadine Bobon, Verena Engelhardt, Lars Erichsen, Norbert W. Paul, Robert Meyer, Fabian Beier, Susann Schweiger, Peter Baumann
description: Vertebrate telomeres, the sequences protecting the end of linear chromosomes, are composed of conserved hexameric GGTTAG repeats. Here we present a C50>A telomerase RNA template mutation that results in the incorporation of the variant telomeric repeat GTTTAG in a family with dyskeratosis congenita primarily presenting as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Tumor necrosis factor-stimulated gene-6 inhibits endoplasmic reticulum stress in the ischemic mouse kidney
creator: Bo Lu, Li Xing, Xiang-Yang Zhu, Hui Tang, Brandon Lu, Fei Yuan, Yazan Almasry, Alexander Krueger, Samer H Barsom, James D Krier, Kyra L Jordan, Amir Lerman, Alfonso Eirin, Lilach O Lerman
description: SummaryKidney tissue injury in renal artery stenosis (RAS) involves inflammation, endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS), and mitochondria damage. Tumor necrosis factor-stimulated gene-6 (TSG-6), an endogenous reparative molecule, may decrease ERS and improve renal function. To assess its impact on the stenotic murine kidney, we injected TSG-6 or vehicle for two weeks in mice with RAS.

title: Comparative analysis of blood trace elements in Egyptian hemodialysis patients and their relatives in the same geographical area, is dialysis still guilty?
creator: Dalia Younis, Ahmed Abd Elwahab, Radwa Sehsah, Mahmoud M. Zakaria, Sameha A. Omar, Ekramy Elmorsy, Mostafa Abdelsalam
description: BackgroundHemodialysis (HD) patients are at theoretical risk for deficiency of essential trace elements and excess potentially toxic elements. The present study aimed to evaluate the influence of environmental and geographical factors on these alterations.MethodsThis comparative cross-sectional study analyzed the blood concentrations of 22 trace elements in 137 participants (HD patients and their relatives) from the same geographical region.

title: Early Postoperative Weight Bearing Following the Reconstruction of Traumatic Complex Tibial Bone Defects by Vascularized Free Fibula and Ilizarov External Fixator: A Case Series
creator: AbdAllah Elgouhary, Mohammed A Sanad, Ahmed I Elgammal, Ahmed Elsayed, Chaitanya Dodakundi, Khalid A Alawadi, Hamed A Badawi
description: Objective: Post-traumatic tibial bone defects represent a significant challenge to orthopedic surgeons. Various reconstructive methods are available based on associated local soft tissue injury and defect size. Free vascularized fibular graft represents a major successful technique; combined with a rigid Ilizarov external fixator, it allows safe, immediate postoperative weight bearing.

title: A secretion-deficient DENV1 DNA vaccine induces durable immunity and confers protection against DENV2
creator: Chen Zhang, Kai-Hao Feng, Yu-Xuan Liu, Chong-Yao Zhong, Kun-Qi Lin, Hui Chen, Dong-Ying Fan, Jing An, Pei-Gang Wang, Na Gao
description: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) remains a major obstacle to dengue virus (DENV) vaccine development and continues to make safe, broadly protective vaccination a global health priority (Aggarwal et al., 2024; Halstead et al., 2014; Martinez et al., 2021; Paz-Bailey et al., 2024; Shepard et al., 2016).

title: Time to extend the indication for sentinel node biopsy in vulvar cancer? Results from a prospective nationwide Swedish study
creator: Diana Zach, Katja Stenström Bohlin, Paivi Kannisto, Louise Moberg, Preben Kjölhede
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectiveTo assess detection rates and negative predictive values of sentinel node biopsy in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with tumors ≥4 cm, multifocal tumors, and in locally recurrent disease.MethodsBetween December 2019 and December 2022, patients with vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with tumors ≥4 cm (group 1), multifocal tumors (group 2), or a first local recurrence without or with previous groin treatment (groups 3 and 4, respectively) were included in a prospective, nationwide multicenter interventional pilot study.

title: Bacterial Vaginosis [BV] knowledge, attitudes and behavioural changes after BV diagnosis among women enrolled in a clinical trial in Boston, USA and Vulindlela, South Africa: a qualitative study
creator: Cecilia Milford, Buyisiwe L Dlamini, Nomfuneko A Mafunda, Timothy S Hardwick, Lara Lewis, Anam A Khan, Makhosazane N Mdladla, Caroline M Mitchell, Disebo Potloane
description: BackgroundBacterial vaginosis (BV), the most common cause of vaginitis among reproductive age women, has high recurrence even after treatment. In addition to the physical risks of BV (e.g. increased HIV risk and adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth), the symptoms (malodour, itchiness, vaginal discharge) can cause emotional impacts (e.g. shame, embarrassment, self-consciousness).

title: Cell autonomous regional differences in oligodendrocyte lineage development and responses to oncohistone H3.3 K27M
creator: Jared M Andrews, Kaitlin M Budd, Chang-Hyuk Kwon, Jon D Larson, Abbas Shirinifard, Lawryn H Kasper, Chanrika C Williams, Alfonso Lavado, Sharon King, Jorge Gutierrez, Daniel Stabley, Tong Lin, Sara A Lewis, Paul A Northcott, Arzu Onar-Thomas, Suzanne J Baker
description: Diffuse midline glioma, H3K27-altered (DMG), is a lethal midline brain tumor. Most DMG, unlike glioma arising in other regions, harbor histone H3.3 K27M (K27M) mutations. The basis for this anatomical selectivity remains unclear. Stem-like DMG cell transcriptomes most resemble oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs).

title: Acute and 14-day effects of tiotropium/olodaterol on cardiopulmonary function in COPD
creator: Thomas Kayser, Nadja Struß, René Pflock, Karsten Heusser, Agilo L. Kern, Andreas Voskrebenzev, Lea Behrendt, Till F. Kaireit, Philipp Badorrek, Jens Tank, Stefan Andreas, Jens Jordan, Jens Vogel-Claussen, Jens M. Hohlfeld
description: BackgroundLung hyperinflation in COPD adversely affects cardiac function and may influence autonomic nervous system activity. The onset of cardiac improvement with dual bronchodilator therapy remains uncertain.MethodsIn this randomised, placebo-controlled, investigator-blinded, mechanistic, single-dose crossover trial with an open-label 2-week extension we assessed tiotropium/olodaterol (T/O) effects on cardiopulmonary function and muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) in hyperinflated COPD patients.

title: The Efficacy of Neuromodulation, Interventional Treatment and Unconventional Therapies in the Treatment of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome: A Systematic Review
creator: Essa A Samuel, Khoula Ahmad, Naelijwa J Manongi, Ramkumar Rajapandian, Sajida Moti wala, Esraa M AlEdani, Safeera Khan
description: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a chronic debilitating multisystem neuropathic pain disorder. It is characterized by continuous pain, usually out of proportion to any known tissue injury, vasomotor changes, sudomotor or edema, and motor or trophic changes. The objective of this study is to assess the efficacy of neuromodulation, interventional, and unconventional treatments for CRPS.

title: Development of a sarcopenic obesity risk prediction model for older adults based on the CHARLS database
creator: Biheng Feng, Yuanyuan Qin, Qingjiang Cai, Debin Huang
description: ObjectiveTo construct a risk prediction model for sarcopenic obesity in the elderly using different machine learning methods.MethodsThe research data were derived from the CHARLS 2015 national survey data. According to the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 2,375 elderly people were selected and 42 research variables were included. The risk factors were screened by univariate analysis.

title: State-dependent binding of the wedge domain controls inactivation of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1
creator: Lucas Roettger, Nadja Zeitzschel, Christian Gorzelanny, Clement Verkest, Stefan G. Lechner
description: The mechanically activated ion channel PIEZO1 transduces membrane tension into intracellular calcium signals and is critical for a wide range of physiological processes. Recent structural and functional studies have established a detailed framework for PIEZO1 activation, but the molecular mechanisms governing its rapid inactivation remain incompletely understood.

title: Beyond spirometry in COPD: expanding the diagnostic paradigm
creator: Surya P. Bhatt, Edwin K. Silverman, James D. Crapo
description: ExtractWe read with great interest the review article by Morelli et al. [1] on diagnostic approaches to COPD. They provide a valuable synthesis of evolving diagnostic paradigms. They highlight the strengths of our recently published multidimensional diagnostic schema that incorporates lung imaging into the diagnostic paradigm [2].

title: Bioactive Effect of Plasma-Rich in Growth Factors (PRGFs) on Cell-Based In Vitro Models of Skin Inflammation in Relation to Inflammatory Skin Disorders
creator: Eduardo Anitua, Roberto Tierno, Zuriñe Martínez de Lagrán, Mohammad H Alkhraisat
description: Plasma rich in growth factors (PRGFs) has proven potentially beneficial as a bioregenerator in patients with chronic skin disorders due to its anti-inflammatory effect. However, its therapeutic potential may be limited by soluble autoimmune components associated with inflammatory dermatoses in blood plasma.

title: Research highlights, The Plant Genome, Volume 16, Issue 4
creator: Unknown

(https://doi.org/10.1002/tpg2.20404) summarize the highlights of articles in the special issue “Epigenome and Epitranscriptome in Plant–Environment Interactions,” which provides new insights into the theoretical basis and technical considerations in investigating epigenetic regulations in different crop species.

title: Hepatitis B and C infections, and co-infections screening among patients attending a tertiary hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: a retrospective database study
creator: Balew Arega, Ermiyas Tefera, Kibrom Mesfin, Daniel Achame, Dawit Tolossa, Abenezer Worku, Ermias Kibru, Nebyu Tafasse, Amdemeskel Mersha
description: BackgroundHepatitis B and C virus infection is a continuous public health problem in Ethiopia, with the prevalence of the disease significantly varying across administrative regions. Determining seroprevalence among people who are unaware of their infection status is essential for hepatitis diagnosis and treatment.

title: Graphite lubricates Mercury’s global contraction
creator: Natalia A VERGARA SASSARINI, Matteo MASSIRONI, Telemaco TESEI, Andrea BISTACCHI
description: Secular cooling of Mercury’s interior drove planetary contraction, forming widespread lobate scarps that are the surface expressions of thrust faults and fold-and-thrust belts. Despite their importance to Mercury’s global tectonics, the mechanics and rheology of these features remain poorly understood.

title: Bullous Pemphigoid Induced by Cefixime: A Rare Side Effect
creator: Nicolas Sandakly, Georgio El Koubayati, Hussein Nassereddine, Fady Haddad
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is the most prevalent autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease of the skin and mucous membranes. This disease typically affects the elderly and manifests with pruritus and localized or, most commonly, generalized bullous lesions. Numerous studies have established the association between BP and oral antidiabetic agents, particularly dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4) inhibitors, diuretics, and certain antibiotics, notably levofloxacin and cephalexin.

title: Evaluation of work life balance and mental states of Eskişehir Tepebaşı municipality employees
creator: Alaettin Ünsal, Mine Tepetaş, Mediha Bal, Didem Arslantaş, Sibel Sert, Selva Dilan Gölbaşı Koç
description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to determine the level of work-life balance of municipal employees, to examine some variables that are thought to be related to it, and to evaluate their mental state. This study is the first known study to assess the work-life balance and mental health of municipal employees.

title: Pneumonia-associated microbial species and stabilized chlorine dioxide–containing oral care products
creator: Hadeel Ayoub, Charu Sharma, Richard L. Gregory
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThis study evaluated the antifungal and antibacterial effects of stabilized chlorine dioxide–containing oral care products against yeast and bacterial species associated with pneumonia.MethodsSix yeast species (Candida albicans, Candida glabrata, Cryptococcus neoformans, Candida dubliniensis, Candida krusei,Candida tropicalis) and 5 bacterial species (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa) were grown in Sabouraud dextrose broth and brain-heart infusion media, respectively, overnight.

title: Keratin 8 enhances the efficacy of mesenchymal stem cells in preventing acute graft-versus-host disease
creator: Ya Zhou, Rui Wang, Zheng Wang, Hao Yu, Qing Xu, Yuxi Xu, Yuxuan He, Ziyi Hu, Qi Wang, Xiaodong Xie, Shijie Yang, Lingyu Zeng, Xiaoqi Wang, Qingxiao Song, Xi Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). The development of methods that preserve graft-versus-leukemia (GVL) activity while preventing aGVHD remains a long-sought goal.

title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1015 EFFECT OF ACUTE INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE ON PLASMA AMYLOID-BETA AND P-TAU217
creator: Francesco Bax, Lei Liu, Elif Gokcal, Mitchell Jacob Horn, Andrew Warren, Adriana Saba, Zahra Shirzadi, Zora Dipucchio, Kristin Schwab, Edip M Gurol, Anand Viswanathan, Jasmeer Chhatwal, Steven Greenberg
description: Background and aimsTo explore the effect of time from intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) on plasma Aβ37, Aβ40, Aβ42, and p-tau217 concentrations in patients with spontaneous ICH due to cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) or hypertension (HTN).MethodsPseudo-longitudinal analysis of a prospective cohort study including patients with acute spontaneous CAA or HTN-related ICH presenting to the Massachusetts General Hospital between 1996 and 2015.

title: 면역관용기에서 면역활동기로 접어드는 HBeAg 양성인 만성 B형간염 환자에서 간세포암종의 발생에 대한 예측모델 개발
creator: Minjong Lee
description: 상시킬 수 있다는 내용이다.2 본 연구는 국내 총 23개 대학병원이 참여한 후향적 다기관 코호트 분석 연구로, 총 3,585명 환자를 분석 대상으로 하였고, 그 주요 기준은 다음과 같다. HBeAg 양성인 만성 B형간염 18세 이상의 성인 환자로 면역관용기에서 면역활동기로 접어들어 엔테카비어 혹은 테노포비어를 시작하게 되었고, 간경변증이 없고, 추적 기간이 1년 이상인 환자를 대상으로 하였다.

title: Seasonal Variations in Birth Patterns in Greece: A Comprehensive Analysis of National Data From 1956 to 2022
creator: Nikolaos Vlachadis, Nikolaos Antonakopoulos, Dionysios N Vrachnis, Nikolaos Loukas, Alexandros Fotiou, Stamatoula Ouzouni, Konstantinos Louis, Christos Parthenis, Marianna Theodora, Nikolaos Vrachnis
description: Introduction: The seasonality of human births has been studied globally for over two centuries, revealing diverse patterns across populations shaped by intricate interactions involving both biological and socio-cultural factors. This study offers a thorough examination of national birth data in Greece spanning from 1956 to 2022, aiming to elucidate long-term trends and changes in seasonal birth patterns.

title: Endogenous green technology innovation and diffusion with strategic international spillovers
creator: Zhuo Feng
description: Escalating environmental challenges necessitate accelerated green technology innovation and diffusion. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework synthesizing differential game theory, endogenous growth with directed technical change, and network analysis to investigate the interplay between strategic national R&D investments, the endogenous direction of innovation, and structured international knowledge spillovers.

title: 3D chromatin dynamics in cellular neuroendocrine transformation
creator: Jianhua Xiong
